feat(workspace): stop a Session's running work before archiving it (#4765)

* feat(workspace): stop a Session's running work before archiving it

Archiving was a pure visibility write, so a Session archived mid-turn kept
running out of sight. The Workspace registry now owns archive admission
through two Host events: `workspace/session-activity` reports what still
runs and refuses the plain archive as `workspace/session-active`;
`workspace/session-stop`, requested with `stopActivity`, stops that work the
way the user's own stop actions do before the archive write. The API Session
Controller reports and stops turns, subagent descendants, and owned jobs and
rejects any model step for an archived Session; the Schedule plugin reports
and deletes active reminders. The sidebar turns the refusal into a
stop-and-archive confirmation listing the Host's answer.

* test(workspace): pin the widened archive signature and prove child liveness by heartbeat

The Client inspect catalog spec pins archiveSession's new options
parameter, and the archive e2e reads the Bash child's liveness from a
heartbeat file instead of a pid: the Linux sandbox runs the tool in its own
PID namespace, so the pid it reports is not comparable from the test.

* test(workspace): cover the archive-admission providers and dialog to the per-file gate

Drop the provider's unused disposer and the dialog's unreachable confirm
guard, read reminders without a catch that no composition can reach, and
add the cases the coverage lane found missing: a stop without a jobs
registry, a looping lineage, a descendant whose projections reject, the
dialog's Escape guard and non-Error reason, and a family merged by another
provider.

* fix(workspace): write the archive before stopping, gate subagent lineage, and delete reminders under the schedule barriers

Review round on #4765. The registry now writes the archive set before it
dispatches `workspace/session-stop`, so the durable set already gates
every wake the stops induce; the controller's `agent/pre-step` gate also
blocks subagent descendants of an archived Session and contains each
cancel or kill on its own. The Schedule plugin's stop listener runs as a
management delete in the agent's transaction queue between the same two
persistence barriers the `schedule_delete` tool uses. The confirm dialog
selects singular or plural English lines and keys list rows by index.
Docs: archive-admission section with type-equiv blocks on the workspace
subsystem page, write-first order and residual windows in the READMEs
and the Agent Note, and the missing zh reminders sentence.

* test(web): scope the question composer's New Session wait to the Sessions tree

The wide sidebar's New Session button carries the same visible label as
a fresh session row, so the unscoped `getByText` either settled on the
button before the row existed or hit a strict-mode violation once the
row rendered first, which is how the snapshots lane failed on
ece68c2ab5. Waiting inside the Sessions tree names the row alone.

* fix(schedule): answer archive admission from the owned runtime's fold, not the projection registry

The `sessionProjections.snapshot` API is the Client projection view and
is not a Host read path (review on #4765). `ScheduleRuntime.activeRecords()`
folds the live log the way every drive does, and the archive-admission
listeners ask the owned runtime for that fold: a session without a live
agent or without an owned runtime has nothing armed to fire, so it reports
nothing and has nothing to stop. Covers the runtime-less agent, a fold that
turns unreadable at the persistence barrier, and the stopping/faulted
runtime answering nothing.

* refactor(subagent): report and stop subagent descendants from the Subagent runtime

The `subagent` family of archive admission moves out of the API Session
Controller into `dsh-subagent`, which records the lineage at delegation
and owns the descriptor (review on #4765): `SubagentRuntime` answers
`workspace/session-activity` with the running descendants, labelled from
each child's descriptor through a live Session observation, and
`workspace/session-stop` by cancelling each of them with the parent
cause. The controller keeps turns, owned jobs, and the lineage step gate,
and composes its provider through `ctx.plugin(SessionActivityProvider)`
with declared injections instead of a bare installer call. `dsh-workspace`
becomes an optional type-only peer of `dsh-subagent`.

* refactor(jobs): answer archive admission for owned jobs from the job registry seam

The `job` family moves out of the API Session Controller into `dsh-jobs`
(review on #4765): the seam's constructor installs the
`workspace/session-activity` and `workspace/session-stop` listeners for
every implementation through the abstract `list` and `kill` alone, so the
controller no longer knows the jobs vocabulary and keeps only the turn
family and the archived-lineage step gate. `dsh-workspace` becomes an
optional type-only peer of `dsh-jobs`.

* refactor(workspace): leave SessionActivityKindMap empty and let each provider merge its family

The workspace package no longer names any activity family (review on
#4765): `SessionActivityKindMap` is empty, and each provider merges its own
key from a module both its faces import — `turn` in the API Session
Controller's types, `job` in the job registry seam's view, `subagent` in
the Subagent runtime's control types, `schedule` in the Schedule plugin's
types. The confirm dialog imports those modules for its cases and keeps
the generic line for any other key; the registry and controller suites
merge test-owned families instead of borrowing the providers'.

* refactor(agent): report and stop the running turn from the Agent registry

The `turn` family moves out of the API Session Controller into `dsh-agent`
(review on #4765): the registry's constructor installs the
`workspace/session-activity` and `workspace/session-stop` listeners for
every Agent it publishes, answering with its own lookup and cancelling the
turn with the user cause, and merges the `turn` key from its client-safe
types. The controller keeps only the archived-lineage step gate, renamed
`ArchivedSessionGate`. `dsh-workspace` becomes an optional type-only peer
of `dsh-agent`; the workspace package depends on none of the providers,
so the edge stays acyclic.

Since #3127 a foreground Bash command is a registered job from its start,
so the archive dialog lists it beside the turn; the e2e and its ARIA golden
expect that row, and the capture keeps the running job by design.

fix(tools): keep surrogate pairs intact when capping tool output

Three tools capped the preview text they return with String.prototype.slice
at a UTF-16 code-unit budget. A cut that lands inside a surrogate pair
leaves a lone high surrogate, which is not well-formed text: a strict JSON
reader rejects the durable Session log carrying it, and the preview shows a
broken glyph. A lone surrogate retained in history has already blocked every
later Messages request for one session.

Centralize the cap in output-retention as
truncateWithoutSplittingSurrogatePair, and use it from the persistent bash
and pwsh shells and the string-replace editor. The cut drops the unpaired
half instead of keeping it, so the retained text stays a prefix and is at
most one code unit shorter than before.

* fix(artifacts): recheck failed DMG detaches before reporting cleanup failure

NativeDmgArtifactReader.close() detached each device once and, when a
detach failed, asked `hdiutil info` once whether the device was still
attached. On APFS images, detaching the synthesized container ejects the
image disk too. `hdiutil info` can still list that ejected device
briefly, and a just-read volume can report busy. Either way a real
cleanup succeeded but close() reported "DMG detach or mount-root cleanup
failed" and kept the mount root.

macOS CI hit this intermittently in verify:macos-bundle: `hdiutil
detach /dev/disk23` failed with "No such file or directory" (already
ejected) and the device was still counted as attached. The #1103
review also raised the missing recheck.

After the first pass, recheck the remaining devices up to three times
with 250/500/1000 ms settle delays. Drop any that hdiutil no longer
lists, retry the detach of any still listed, and fail only for devices
that stay attached. The host seam gains an optional delay so tests run
without real waits.

fix(doctor): migrate hosted Ollama provider references (#168782)

## What Problem This Solves

Older Cloud-only Ollama setup stored `https://ollama.com` under `models.providers.ollama`. After the dedicated `ollama-cloud` provider was introduced, those configurations and their cron/session references still selected the local provider.

## User Impact

Doctor moves only the `ollama` entry whose URL origin is exactly `https://ollama.com`, including case, path, trailing-slash, and default-port variants. Localhost, LAN, custom endpoints, other provider keys, and local-daemon cloud models remain unchanged. An existing `ollama-cloud` provider keeps its authored settings and gains missing catalog entries.

Matching model references move with the provider. Their `@profile` suffix is removed rather than guessing which Cloud account to use; one Doctor note explains how to re-pin. This migration does not inspect or change saved credentials. Environment-backed URLs, API-key templates, and SecretRefs retain their authored references.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama plugin declares the routing migration through its existing Doctor contract. The shared model-reference walker handles config and cron references; the existing session owner handles model/provider pairs and saved fallback/rollback routes. Preflight leaves the hosted entry intact. The config writer repairs persisted references first, then publishes config last. An interrupted run retains the hosted source entry as its retry signal; a completed migration never replays backups onto later local selections.

### Simplification

Removed saved-account discovery, per-agent/shared account selection, auth-profile remapping, the config walker’s per-agent split, agent-ID threading, per-reference session reporting, unused test API surface, and the separate lint-preview path. Consolidated duplicate auth/state fixtures into focused regressions.

Against merge base `e40606fdea96135758ec5bc0b1a355d08ead0c7e`, production is **+542/-78 lines** and tests/test support are **+714/-1 lines** (including two harness lines). The earlier candidate added about 830 production and 1,650 test lines. Documentation is +44/-1; the existing mock-export baseline shrinks by two entries.

The remaining non-core changes have specific owners:

- Config planning carries the matched declaration to the writer so state repair precedes config publication.
- Reference restoration applies the resolved routing decision to authored templates so renamed environment-backed URLs and credentials stay templates.
- Health runners retain readonly/legacy-handoff guards before state repair and publish config only after all state repairs succeed.
- Registry/module/SDK changes load and validate plugin-owned declarations. Compatibility execution stays in the existing compatibility module: adding declaration loading exceeds the registry’s 700-line limit without that split. Compatibility preflight itself does not perform the rename.
- Removed the speculative URL-userinfo/scheme restriction on plugin-authored rename declarations. Declarations still require valid provider IDs and a parseable URL; migration matching compares origins, which never include userinfo. The Ollama declaration and runtime matching are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused coverage passes **48 tests across five files**. Core and extension typechecks, affected test typecheck graphs (`plugins-platform`, `commands-doctor`), scoped core/extension lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass. The migration runtime build at `391cefd415a2` passes; the later validator-only change was checked through focused declaration/registry tests and lint.

fix(compaction): stop a failed summary audit from leaving a session permanently uncompactable (#130393)

* fix(compaction): stop a failed summary audit from leaving a session uncompactable

Once a session reaches this state it cannot leave it. Compaction runs, produces a
summary, fails its quality audit, and cancels. Nothing shrinks, so the next turn is
larger than the last and fails the same way, and every later turn ends in "Context
is too large and auto-compaction could not recover this turn". The only escape is
/new, which discards the conversation.

Cancelling is right for a summary that is merely bad: it preserves history rather
than storing something worse. It is wrong when the audit cannot be satisfied at
all, because the session can then never shrink and the user loses the whole
conversation instead of some fidelity.

Both terminal quality paths - an exhausted audit and required facts that cannot fit
the finalized budget - now emit the structured previous summary plus the preserved
recent turns and the generated split-turn prefix through one degradeToFallbackSummary
closure, and let compaction complete. Genuinely unrecoverable paths still cancel: a
failed built-in generation, an unresolvable summarization model, and missing
credentials.

The degradation is recorded on the boundary it produced, as details.qualityDegraded,
not only in a log line. Reading intent back out of the fallback template's prose is
the multi-signal inference this repo's doctrine forbids, and the log line is not
durable. parseCompactionDetails carries the flag across the read path so the fact
survives a reload.

Corrects a contract the code stated and the tests asserted. A configured compaction
provider that throws does NOT cancel: the exception is caught and falls back to
built-in summarization, so the comment naming "LLM throw" as the path that still
cancels described the wrong route. What actually reaches the degrade is a summarizer
that SUCCEEDS and then fails the audit. Traced against production: rh-bot 2026-09-07
lost every gpufarm backend mid-compaction, summarizeViaLLM threw, and the outer catch
cancelled 298 messages with history preserved - the throw path behaving correctly.

agent-session-compaction table now names a closed outcome per row - recovered,
degraded, cancelled - instead of a boolean that conflated "not recovered" with
"cancelled"; only caller cancellation leaves history untouched. The
retention-infeasible test asserts the degraded commit. The compact.hooks provenance
row asserts the recorded flag on the persisted boundary.

when validation is exhausted, which is no longer true.

fix: configured model fallbacks are skipped when the primary model times out (#141869)

* fix(agents): give each model fallback attempt its own run budget

A chat/agent run's whole-run deadline is sized for ONE attempt:
`registerChatAbortController` sets `expiresAtMs` to `timeoutMs` plus a 60s
abort grace, and `resolveAgentTimeoutMs` feeds that same `timeoutMs` to the
per-attempt CLI timer. A primary candidate that times out has therefore already
spent the entire run budget, so every later fallback candidate inherits only
the grace window. `runGatewayMaintenance` sweeps the entry, aborts the
controller with `createChatAbortSignalReason("timeout")` — an external, bare
`TimeoutError` — and the fallback chain stops without reaching the configured
tail.

`markExecutionStarted` refreshes the deadline once, and returns early for
`kind !== "agent"`, so a `chat-send` run never gets even that one refresh.

This renews the deadline as each attempt actually starts, in the attempt layer
next to the existing "later attempts must not start after an abort" guard. The
run owner registers a renewer keyed by run id; runs with no registered owner
(CLI, cron, unit tests) keep today's behavior exactly.

The renewal only ever extends, never shortens, and declines for a registration
that is missing, superseded, aborted, not yet executing, or already past its
deadline — an entry the sweep has condemned is never revived. Abort attribution
is untouched: this changes WHEN the run deadline fires, never HOW an abort is
classified. The once-only guard in `markExecutionStarted` is untouched.

The deadline resolvers move to `src/gateway/chat-run-deadline.ts` alongside the
renewal; `chat-abort.ts` re-exports them, so existing import paths are
unchanged.

Worst case run wall clock becomes `attempts x timeoutSeconds + grace` instead
of `timeoutSeconds + grace`. That is the point: the configured chain cannot
otherwise complete. No new config knob; `timeoutSeconds: 0` already exists for
callers that want no run budget at all.

* fix(gateway): keep the run-deadline module a type-graph leaf

check:madge-import-cycles rejected chat-abort.ts -> chat-run-deadline.ts ->
chat-abort.ts. The back-edge was a single type-only import, so
check:import-cycles still reported 0 runtime value cycles; only the type graph
was circular.

renewChatRunExecutionDeadline reads controller and executionStarted and writes
expiresAtMs. Declaring exactly that shape locally as ChatRunDeadlineEntry drops
the back-edge without a new file, and ReadonlyMap states that the entry map is
never structurally mutated here.

* fix(infra): drop the test-only deadline renewer reset

deadcode:full flagged resetAgentRunDeadlineRenewersForTest as an unused export,
since knip runs --production and a helper only a test imports never reaches the
production graph.

It was never needed. removeChatAbortControllerEntry already calls
unregisterAgentRunDeadlineRenewer, so the test can retire its registration
through the same path the gateway uses. Moving that into afterEach also makes
cleanup survive a failing assertion, which the inline reset did not.

file fails the gate. Confirmed by moving the file aside: the check passes at

* fix(agents): renew the run deadline only for recovery attempts

Review finding: renewal ran before every candidate, including the primary,
so a finite whole-run timeout could be extended even by a run that never
reaches a fallback. Gate the call on attempt > 1.

A configuration with no fallback candidates, or one whose primary succeeds,

candidate that follows a failed attempt is given a fresh budget, which is

This also closes the regression-test hole the review named: with the primary

callback and asserts it is unchanged from admission, then asserts the

fix(telegram): redeliver saved final text after ambiguous network failures (#168738)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram final answers being replaced by a delivery warning after an ambiguous network failure, even though the completed answer is already saved.

## User Impact

Telegram automatically re-delivers a saved ordinary text or rich-text final once, without running the model or completed tools again. A rare duplicate answer is possible when Telegram accepted the original send but its response was lost.

Media, interactive or side-effect payloads, tool-initiated sends, known accepted chunks, identityless results, and untyped failures retain the existing no-blind-replay behavior. Other channels remain default-off. There is no new user setting or database schema.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Maintainer decision:** reverse the automatic-resend exclusion in #155906 only for ordinary Telegram text finals, accepting the duplicate tradeoff. Preserve its accepted-content, partial-delivery, and visible-failure invariants. The proven-pre-connect recovery from #101024 remains unchanged.

Telegram explicitly opts into the shared durable-delivery contract. The existing queue owns the saved prepared payload, exact send-attempt claim, two-attempt budget, backoff, recovery, and completion. The original caller waits for that recovery before reporting failure. Transcript-correlation metadata remains eligible without admitting controls; retries retain live authority checks and the last attempt's partial-delivery evidence. Transport diagnostics retain only bounded cause codes/syscalls, not request data.

After exhaustion, the notice is `I couldn't deliver my reply because of a network problem. Please ask again.` when a typed network cause exists; otherwise it is `I couldn't deliver my reply. Please ask again.`

Slack owner changes #151069 and #132928 do not overlap this diff. Follow-ups for Discord, Slack, and other channels must assess each transport's reconciliation and duplicate-prevention contract before opting in; this PR does not enable them.

## Evidence

### Real Telegram Test Server, live model

All cases use the same isolated Gateway configuration: streaming off, rich messages enabled, a leased real-user observer, and a proxy that changes only the selected Bot API response. Each case records 90 seconds. Each candidate case made **one primary model request**; two auxiliary model requests and three embedding requests were tracked separately. No tools were requested or rerun.

| Case | Userbot sent message | Observed replies | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main before-forward drop | `83211845632` | `83212894208`: `I couldn't confirm the reply reached Telegram. Check OpenClaw chat history for the answer before retrying the task.` | No answer; only the old notice. |
| Candidate before-forward drop | `83219185664` | `83220234240`: `SAVED_FINAL_repaired-before` | Saved answer automatically delivered; no failure notice. |
| Candidate forward-then-drop | `83221282816` | `83222331392` and `83223379968`: both `SAVED_FINAL_repaired-duplicate` | First send was accepted upstream (HTTP 200, `ok:true`), then its response was lost; exactly one duplicate appeared, no third reply or notice. |
| Candidate without fault | `83224428544` | `83225477120`: `SAVED_FINAL_repaired-plain` | One ordinary reply, no retry or notice. |

The sent text in each row was `Reply with exactly <marker> and nothing else. Do not use tools.`, using the matching `SAVED_FINAL_<case>` marker. Baseline marker: `SAVED_FINAL_baseline-proof`. The before-forward proxy consumed the complete final-send request without forwarding it; the duplicate case forwarded it and discarded the accepted response.

Baseline source: `f0a64d10805d2e7e21b4fa45235d8074a95e033d`. Candidate runtime: one immutable build of `2e2238f953bcd3c824e22384132d8e16c5977da3`, reused for all three cases. The final head adds a type-safe guard around transport diagnostic inspection, removes two invalid test-fixture variants, fixes a redundant type argument and a shadowed local name, and rebases onto green main; those changes do not alter the exercised reply path. No `dist/` copy or model stub was used.

### Regression and compatibility proof

- The main-branch real final-delivery negative control fails because its caller settles before saved-text recovery.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a model listed by `models list --refresh` failing its first `agent --local` turn with `Unknown model` when the provider is authenticated but has no configured model.

## User Impact

After signing in and refreshing the local catalog, users can run newly listed models without adding hand-written provider/model configuration. Gateway-backed listing remains Gateway-backed. Without a prior refresh, an unknown model still tells the user to run `models list --refresh --provider <id>`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two disconnected paths caused the failure: the catalog worker deliberately plans discovery without persisting it, and static runtime preparation omitted persisted catalogs for credential-only providers. Keep the worker read-only, as introduced by 1cb9f70 (catalog discovery isolation). For an offline CLI refresh, hold exclusive local-state custody and use the existing live standalone catalog preparation, which writes the existing per-agent SQLite catalog cache. Project those same admitted facts rather than starting a second refresh. Keep managed-proxy setup and cleanup around discovery.

Static runtime preparation now includes catalog owners for current credentials, using the existing registry reader and resolver. Removed credentials do not admit credential-only cached models. No schema, configuration, or additional storage format changes.

Explicit offline refresh carries the existing 180-second discovery budget through standalone preparation; ordinary preparation retains its 5-second default. The enclosing generation allows that discovery budget in addition to normal preparation time.

Maintainer-intent check: no matching changes in the touched files.

- Regression failed on the original code: a persisted-only model resolved to `undefined`. The candidate passes both current-credential and removed-credential cases.
- 53 focused tests pass across catalog sources, catalog ownership, and CLI listing, including Gateway routing and proxy cleanup. The acquisition-boundary regression holds a provider for 125.1 seconds of virtual time, verifies exactly one discovery, and checks the resulting SQLite row. Before the budget fix, the provider timed out and the list was empty.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes machine enrollment silently running an old cached npm release when the Gateway is newer.

## User Impact

`devices join-code` and the Control UI now suggest the Gateway's published npm version, not the invoking CLI's version. Both also show the short alternative for an existing OpenClaw installation. The default remains a background service with explicit session-host consent; command-only services remain available.

Source checkouts and unpublished builds prefer a resolvable matching channel tag. If npm cannot confirm a target, the command stays unpinned and a one-line note asks for a matching Gateway build. JSON keeps `joinUrl` and `command`, adding `serviceCommand`, `installedCommand`, and optional `versionNote`.

## Why This Change Was Made

[#168623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168623) / `8f91e4bb65f` established the one-paste service/session-host default but deliberately left npm unpinned. npm can reuse an old cached package. The Gateway now owns version selection and command formatting in the same RPC that mints the URL; CLI and UI consume its commands instead of independently rebuilding them.

The existing update owners supply install identity and channel policy. Joining does not run a full update/dependency inspection. This composes with the durable service installation work in [#168644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168644); it does not change node execution, service lifecycle, or upgrade commands.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

- Real isolated Gateway text/JSON: baseline printed unpinned npm commands; candidate printed `openclaw@2026.9.9`, matching the Gateway release, plus the existing-installation alternative. Both exited successfully. This proof exercises command generation, not installation on a second machine; durable service installation is covered separately by #168644.
- The built CLI bootstrap guard passed. The local changed gate stopped at an unrelated existing mock-export violation in `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection-placement.test.ts`; the rebase picked up its existing `mock-isolation` explanation. Hosted exact-head CI is the final check.

fix(node): keep npx-installed services outside the npm cache (#168644)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes node services installed through `npx openclaw connect <join-url> --service` or `npx openclaw node install` pointing at npm's disposable `_npx` cache.

## User Impact

The one-paste command installs the selected OpenClaw release into a durable npm prefix under the node's state directory before writing the service. Removing npm's exec cache no longer removes the service's executable. Installation prints the package version, chosen runtime, service command, and a fresh-npx node update command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service argument resolver previously used the running package's resolved path. #167905 fixes pnpm's replaceable store-generation paths by selecting its existing stable link; npm exec has no stable link to select. This preserves that pnpm behavior and adds node-install promotion through the existing npm update owners (`resolveGlobalInstallTarget`, `runGlobalPackageUpdateSteps`, and their staged publication/rollback/cleanup).

There is one `<state-dir>/npm` prefix, not a prefix per release. The normal state-directory/profile resolver chooses its location. Run `npx -y openclaw@latest node install --force` on the node to update it, retaining the same profile/state-directory settings. An exact version or `@beta` can replace `@latest`. Reinstalling an already-selected version repairs damaged package files. No new settings or package manager.

This does not change `openclaw update` or its existing co-located Gateway selection behavior. Node auto-update still follows the node's npm channel, not the connected Gateway's version/build. fix(skills): background skill reviews run after every turn that uses a learned skill (#168679)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: background Skill Workshop reviews (and their "💾 Learned" notices) run right after almost every turn in a conversation that keeps using a learned skill.

## User Impact

User impact: reviews now run only after 10 accumulated model iterations in a session, so skill-heavy conversations get a review every ~10 iterations instead of after each turn. A turn that changed a learned skill itself still resets the count. The skills a turn used still inform the review when it runs.

fix(node): keep paired credentials after service enrollment (#168653)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes paired nodes failing to authenticate after `openclaw connect <join-url> --service` when the machine already has credentials for another Gateway.

## User Impact

A node reconnecting to its saved Gateway uses its paired device token instead of an unrelated Gateway token or password from the machine's environment, configuration, or state-directory `.env`. Paired service installations no longer persist those ambient credentials.

Intentional shared-token/password connections remain supported through `openclaw node run --auth-from-env` and `openclaw node install --auth-from-env --force`. This exposes the existing foreground override and records that explicit choice for installed services. If it displaces an available paired credential, the warning names the selected environment variable, never its value. No new configuration keys or token migration are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node credential owner already recognized a saved pairing but still treated every populated `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` / `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` as an explicit override. The service planner also persisted those ambient values. Environment variables loaded from `env.vars` or the state-directory `.env` therefore had the same effect as an intentional override.

The runtime and service planner now share the same saved-endpoint eligibility check. Default reconnects leave device-token selection and refresh with `GatewayClient`; explicit shared auth uses the existing environment-only path. GatewayClient's trusted-endpoint retry policy is unchanged.

This retains the intent of [#31122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/31122) (intentional service environment credentials survive restarts), [#136253](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136253) (a co-located Gateway must not displace paired-node auth), and [#159360](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159360) (expired fallback setup codes may only resume the saved pairing; no expired bootstrap or shared-auth fallback).

## Evidence

- On baseline `e40606fdea9`, an isolated Gateway issued a real join URL and a second isolated machine state completed bootstrap pairing through `connect --service`. The first handshake of the restarted real install-plan command failed authentication for process-env token, process-env password, config `env.vars`, and state-directory `.env`. All four sources were persisted into the service environment. CWD `.env` was already blocked by workspace policy; plain co-located `gateway.auth.*` was already correctly skipped.
- The repaired replay connected on the first handshake for all six sources, without persisting any ambient token/password. The explicit `--auth-from-env` shared-token control also connected, retained its selected credential in the generated service environment, and retained the explicit service argument.

  | Credential source | Baseline first handshake | Repaired first handshake | Repaired ambient credential persisted |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Process token | Auth rejection | Connected | No |
  | Process password | Auth rejection | Connected | No |
  | Config `env.vars` token | Auth rejection | Connected | No |
  | State-directory `.env` token | Auth rejection | Connected | No |
  | CWD `.env` token | Connected (already blocked) | Connected | No |
  | Co-located `gateway.auth.*` | Connected (already skipped) | Connected | No |
  | Explicit shared-token flag | — | Connected | Yes, intentionally |

fix: explain unavailable Codex sessions on paired devices (#168641)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the New Session device picker explains a missing Codex harness as an opaque node-command failure when an OpenAI model cannot run on a paired laptop.

## User Impact

The reason now explains the model/harness/device relationship first, then gives the node-side install, enable, restart, and approval steps. Users can also choose a model using the OpenClaw harness. It says **unavailable**, rather than incorrectly claiming every disabled or denied plugin is uninstalled.

There is no automatic installation, silent harness substitution, or change to node/Gateway approval policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex is an official external plugin, not part of the stock npm node package. A source checkout can also contain the plugin without enabling it on the node. The existing node-local plugin loader already declares `codex.exec-server.stdio.v1` only when the plugin is present and enabled; the new integration coverage preserves missing, explicitly disabled, explicitly denied, and enabled cases. No second capability or availability owner is needed.

The shared required-command authority owns the explanation used by both device discovery and placement. Pending pairing approval and Gateway policy denial keep their existing, distinct remedies.

Provenance:
- [#88451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88451) introduced the unified OpenAI implicit Codex default (`4c33aaa86c1`); [#104685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104685) moved effective-route policy into the provider (`1b1cebfe421`). Both were located with `git log -S`.
- [#127202](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127202) introduced the approved paired-device exec-server command (`1353ce0995c`).
- [`d111676bcbf`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d111676bcbfec4313ffd8707596d96875eac09bf) deliberately excluded Codex from the root npm package. This PR preserves that distribution decision.
- Inspected upstream Codex `codex-rs/cli/src/exec_server_command.rs` at `c248f6d48b97eb4a2aa56147a0b11b7d763278b9`: stdio execution is native; remote registration/auth is a separate branch. OpenClaw's plugin owns the pinned binary; the ordinary node does not need a separate Codex login to advertise the command.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the changed files.

## Evidence

- Regression through the real `environments.list` handler: the new harness explanation assertion fails on `e40606fdea9` with the old command-first message (1 failed / 5 passed), and passes after the fix.
- Focused checks: 33 tests passed across the real node plugin-loader integration, node-command policy, and environment-command authority suites. The node integration loads the actual Codex plugin, not a replacement registration fixture.
- Rebased cleanly onto `f3af0db8fce`, including main's repair for the earlier duplicate-import failure. Full CI is green on `bb4428fc20492b523f42d812987261c74d27c138`: 57 passed, 54 skipped, no failures or pending checks; [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38089723977/job/114324791021).

- Actual Control UI before/after captures with deterministic Gateway fixtures, inspected on macOS arm64. The device stays disabled in both images; the improvement is the truthful explanation and recovery choices. The after fixture obtains its message from the production authority function. These are visual reproduction captures, not a live-model execution claim.

improve: default device joins to session-host services (#168623)

## What Problem This Solves

Newly joined machines default to a foreground, command-only node, while New Session gives already-paired devices an invalid reconnect command and misleadingly says no session hosts are paired.

## User Impact

The CLI and Control UI now offer `npx -y openclaw connect <join-url> --service --session-host` by default. It installs a background node service that can run agent sessions, with a command-only service alternative. The UI shows the full command instead of clipping its consent flags.

Session hosting remains an explicit device-local choice in the pasted command; the node runtime's default is unchanged. Use hosting only on trusted shared Gateway infrastructure.

Already-paired devices get the supported `openclaw config set nodeHost.workerRuns.enabled true`, then `openclaw node install --force` instructions. The empty-host hint distinguishes pairing from enabling hosting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserves the one-paste, single-use onboarding contract from [#122499](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122499) and [#122635](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122635). Corrects the remediation introduced in [#145183](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145183) using the saved-pairing service path documented by [#159810](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159810).

The join handler is its own lazy CLI module rather than adding more responsibilities to the device-management runtime. `-y` only skips [npm's package-install confirmation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npx/); it does not replace OpenClaw consent. No package version is pinned.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Regressions fail on baseline `7e23f938f80590889e459de098f75cbfbdbfc686` for CLI text/JSON and paired-host/empty-host rendering.
- Real CLI before/after proof used separate isolated Gateways and state directories: the baseline printed `npx openclaw connect <url>`; the candidate printed the service/session-host command and command-only alternative. Both JSON invocations exited 0.
- CLI and lazy-loading tests: 52 passed. The Gateway setup and three UI rendering/picker suites pass after the scope reduction, as does the host-only browser regression. The five connection-dialog browser flows also pass.
- Independent exact-head review: **LAND**, no findings.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38083704554): **success**, 46 successful jobs, none failed or cancelled.
- [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168623#issuecomment-6101771154): **ready** on `d456a0ebad0fb6bd101821f0f8839896a7fde7f0`, no findings.
- Local `check:changed` passed its ratchets and core/test/UI typechecks, then stopped at the global unused-export scan. The same model-auth and Solid lint exports fail on clean `origin/main` (`e40606fdea96`); the additional pre-existing Solid test-helper export has already been removed upstream in [62629b0d6ee](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62629b0d6ee). None of these files are changed here.

fix(models): honor live thinking levels in agent runs (#168566)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent runs that reject a thinking level the provider now supports, or accept a level the provider has removed, when an older model row already declares `reasoning`.

## User Impact

Agent commands, replies, and scheduled runs use the thinking levels in their admitted provider catalog. This reads the catalog already held in memory; it does not fetch a model list during a turn. Explicit configured level maps and effort lists still win. Missing observations do not mean that thinking is unsupported.

xAI sign-in no longer saves provider-owned effort lists or thinking maps as operator overrides. Sign in again to replace rows saved by an older sign-in. Other model fields and credentials retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A defined `reasoning` boolean does not prove that the supported level list is current. Remove that short circuit from command selection and fallback execution, and from these five consumers:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/model-runtime-normalization.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts`

The existing catalog owner still controls observation, route selection, and lifetime. Re-sign-in persistence is owned by `extensions/xai/onboard.ts::applyXaiOAuthConfig`. The shared ID-keyed auth merge preserves omitted model fields, so merely leaving out the old effort list did not delete it from saved config. xAI now supplies explicit `undefined` deletion markers for its thinking map and effort list. Other providers keep their existing merge behavior; no config migration is needed.

## Evidence

- Command and reply regressions both fail with the old guard for an added level and a removed level. They pass with this change.
- The full `runModelsAuthLoginFlowCore` regression fails on the prior head because copied thinking fields survive the disk write. It passes with the xAI deletion markers and confirms another provider's explicit map and effort list remain unchanged.
- 268 tests passed across the two reported failure files and the focused command, reply, cron, catalog-owner, and xAI suites. Coverage includes explicit overrides, missing observations, native runtime selection, and no-network catalog reads.
- The source build completed through the normal CLI wrapper.
- An isolated Anthropic API-key profile refreshed its catalog, then completed `agent --local --thinking max` and returned `OK` with HTTP 200. Its configured model row had only the reasoning boolean, not a level map. The live listing supplied `max`. The redacted outgoing request contained:

```json
{
  "model": "<live-listed Anthropic model>",
  "thinking": { "type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized" },
  "output_config": { "effort": "max" }
}
```

## Upgrade compatibility proof

`npm view openclaw version` reported **2026.9.9**. The proof executed that published package's `applyXaiOAuthConfig` and saved its JSON output, including the copied `["low", "high"]` effort list. No real xAI account was used: a local HTTP server supplied synthetic OAuth credentials, a model listing, and streamed API responses.

The candidate loaded those bytes through the normal config loader. An embedded `--thinking high` turn returned `OK`. The real `runModelsAuthLoginFlowCore` then completed sign-in against the stub, and a fresh read of the saved file contained neither `thinkingLevelMap` nor `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`. The config still validated. After catalog refresh, `--thinking xhigh` returned `OK`.

Redacted trace:

```json
[
  {"stage":"stable-config","version":"2026.9.9","supportedReasoningEfforts":["low","high"]},
  {"stage":"candidate-load","valid":true},
  {"request":"/v1/responses","model":"grok-4.6","reasoning":{"effort":"high","summary":"auto"},"reply":"OK"},
  {"oauth":["/.well-known/openid-configuration","/oauth2/device/code","/oauth2/token","/v1/models"]},
  {"stage":"saved-config-readback","thinkingLevelMap":"absent","supportedReasoningEfforts":"absent","reasoning":true,"valid":true},
  {"request":"/v1/responses","model":"grok-4.6","reasoning":{"effort":"xhigh","summary":"auto"},"reply":"OK"}
]
```

This profile had no Gateway. Sign-in reported the local Gateway refresh warning, but the saved-config readback and both embedded turns succeeded without a restart.

## Review follow-ups

- Keyless host selection with plugins disabled must remain available after an explicit runtime reset. That is a real contract: runtime preparation now skips the provider-catalog lookup when plugins are disabled. It does not grant explicit model availability.
- The fallback test's ban on a scoped read pinned the old guard, not a network boundary. It now returns no observation for the fallback provider and still checks that the prepared fallback metadata selects `xhigh`. It also checks the scope of all three in-memory reads.

Core behavior can be reverted. Re-signing into xAI removes copied capability fields from saved rows; reverting does not restore those removed values. The affected surface is thinking selection for agent runs and xAI sign-in, not transport routing or credentials.

OpenCode Zen hides listed models when public metadata is missing, omits OpenClaw attribution on discovery and supported request transports, and tells users to sign in again when a free model is limited to OpenCode's own client.

## User Impact

- Listed Zen chat models appear without an OpenClaw update, even before public metadata arrives. Known model metadata and lifecycle filters still apply.
- Native Zen discovery and model requests on the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic transports send `User-Agent: openclaw/<version>`. Custom proxy URLs do not inherit this header. The `google-generative-ai` SDK path does not yet apply this policy and remains a follow-up. Go behavior is unchanged.
- A `403 FreeTierError` explains the provider's client restriction and marks only that model unavailable. It does not cool down the credential for other models. A `402` still tells the user to check the account balance.

This does not bypass free-tier restrictions or grant account credit. No config, schema, protocol, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Zen uses the existing listed-row projection seam added for Go. Rows without metadata use Zen's native OpenAI-compatible route and default limits. The shared non-chat filter still removes embedding rows. There is no `test` blacklist or `-free` name rule.

The authenticated listing returned 42 IDs. The only IDs without public metadata were `jev-1.13`, `jev-1.13-free`, and `test`. Their raw rows had no price, tier, or free flag:

```json
[
  {"id":"jev-1.13-free","object":"model","created":1791655624,"owned_by":"opencode"},
  {"id":"test","object":"model","created":1791655624,"owned_by":"opencode"},
  {"id":"jev-1.13","object":"model","created":1791655624,"owned_by":"opencode"}
]
```

The listing is the model-existence source. Access failures belong to the request result, not a guessed name filter. Attribution uses the existing policy owner and manifest endpoint facts. Error copy uses the existing status and structured-error parser; it does not expose the raw provider body.

## Evidence

- Main-base regressions failed for missing Zen attribution and misleading free-tier copy. The catalog regression failed before the projection change because listed IDs without metadata were absent. The model-level refusal regression also failed before adding the Zen classification hook. The updated Zen plugin suite (26 tests) and shared model-cooldown suite (34 tests) pass; the attribution (16) and user-facing error (42) suites passed before the plugin-only follow-up.
- Live authenticated requests with honest OpenClaw attribution:

  | Model | Status | Result |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `jev-1.13` | 402 | `server_error`: `Upstream request failed: Insufficient account funds` |
  | `jev-1.13-free` | 403 | `FreeTierError`: free tier is limited to the OpenCode client |
  | `test` | 403 | The same `FreeTierError` restriction |

- Gateway regression: before the classification fix, a `test` turn returned 403 and put the shared credential into auth cooldown; the next paid-model turn was blocked. After the fix, an isolated Gateway on loopback port 18980 classified the same 403 as `model_not_found`, preserved the client-restriction message, and sent the next `jev-1.13` turn upstream 19 seconds later on the same credential. That request returned 402 with account-balance guidance, not a cooldown error. Refresh also returned 41 active Zen rows, including all three IDs. No successful generation is claimed for this unfunded account.
- Captured discovery and model requests sent `User-Agent: openclaw/2026.9.9`; authorization was redacted. Model requests retained `x-opencode-session`.
- The source build completed. The changed-file check stopped at the existing environment-variable budget failure, 456 names against 455; the same failure is present on main. This change adds no environment variables.

Reverting this change restores the prior behavior; it writes no new state format. The affected surface is native Zen discovery, request identity on OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic transports, and model-level refusal classification, plus safe copy for structured `403 FreeTierError` responses. Custom endpoints, Google SDK attribution, and Go keep their current behavior.

fix(ai): stream completions text live when reasoning precedes it (#150685)

* fix(ai): stream completions text live when reasoning precedes it

Since #125149 any OpenAI-completions stream that carries native reasoning
hides every byte of visible text until the stream ends: the first reasoning
chunk marks the message terminal-bound and arms the reasoning-tag partitioner's
strict mode, and text sharing a chunk with reasoning is routed through the
tag-aware path, which also arms strict mode. With a reasoning model on vLLM
the answer therefore arrives as one delta at the end, minutes after the
reasoning finished, even though the server streamed it token by token.

That deferral exists so text interrupted by resumed reasoning can be
classified as commentary or final answer at terminal. Reasoning that precedes
every visible byte leaves nothing to reclassify, so defer only when reasoning
resumes after visible text: mark the message terminal-bound and switch the
partitioner to strict mode only then, and route same-chunk text through the
tag-aware path only once the message is terminal-bound. Resumed-reasoning
streams behave exactly as before.

Measured against vLLM (qwen38-flash-next, reasoning low): before, one
2,924-character text delta at 16.8 s; after, 92 deltas starting 50 ms after
the last thinking delta.

Stream visible Chat Completions text through initial and resumed reasoning while keeping final delivery limited to the confirmed answer. Preserve unfinished reasoning-tag privacy and content followed only by reasoning.

fix(ollama): reuse prompt prefixes across subagent spawns (#164804)

* perf(context): keep the prompt prefix append-only on cacheable routes

A route that caches its prompt prefix, or continues from a stored response, re-prefills
everything from the first changed token. The runner strips historical runtime-context
carriers by default for OpenAI-compatible routes, which shifts every later item (tool
definitions included) as soon as a turn becomes history: the prefix then only matches up
to the system prompt and the whole tail is recomputed on every turn.

Treat these routes like the existing Claude-thinking-prefix case and keep their runtime
context append-only. Native OpenAI-family extensions already do this unconditionally; this
covers the shared helper used by provider plugins and the fallback used by config-defined
providers, which so far only opted in for prefix-binding Claude models.

Measured on a local engine whose prefix cache is compared byte-for-byte: a continuation
turn's reuse went from 7,680 to 10,752 of ~10,900 prompt tokens, and the re-prefilled
remainder from 3,252 tokens (~10.0 s) to 130 (~1.5 s).

Opt-in per model, so routes that do not declare the capability keep today's behavior.

* fix(context): keep a subagent's system prompt identical across spawns

A child session key carries a fresh id per spawn, and it was rendered into the system
prompt twice: in the Runtime line and in the "## Session Context" block. Two children of
the same shape therefore shipped different prompts, so no provider-side prompt cache could
be reused for them.

Measured locally with two identical spawns: they shared only the first 8,104 of ~10,900
prompt tokens, leaving ~3,250 tokens (about 10 s) to re-prefill per spawn. After moving the
per-spawn identity into the task message and rendering the Runtime line's session from a
scope with volatile cron/dashboard/subagent ids removed, the two prompts are byte-identical
and the same spawns reuse 10,752 tokens with 130 left to prefill (~1.5 s).

The child still receives its label and session key; they now travel in the task message,
which is not part of the cacheable prefix.

* fix(context): gate the fallback to Responses and key the policy cache by capability

Two defects from review of the append-only change:

* The unowned-provider fallback enabled append-only context for any non-Google compatible
  route, including `openai-completions`, while the shared Responses helper restricts the
  same gate to the Responses family and the new test asserts Chat Completions is unchanged.
  A custom Chat Completions setup would have retained old carriers and inbound metadata
  where the equivalent plugin-owned route stays transient. Gate the fallback identically.
* `resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoizes by config/provider/model identity, but this policy now
  depends on the model's capability flags. With one config, resolving an unflagged model and
  then an opted-in model returned the first policy, so the result depended on resolution
  order. Include the effective capability predicate in the key, as the existing
  reasoning-compat inputs already do, and cover both orders.

Verified: tsgo rc=0; `src/agents/transcript-policy.test.ts` passes, and the both-order case
fails when only the cache-key line is reverted.

fix(agents): use ChatGPT routes for isolated Codex completions (#168552)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: isolated and utility completions can require an OpenAI API key even when the selected model is available through the user's ChatGPT sign-in.

Related: #168033.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex utility completions can use the same subscription route as the model picker. Explicit auth profiles and utility-model overrides remain in force. A missing pinned profile fails instead of using another account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status path used the first logical catalog row. Dispatch used the resolved model's transport. Either row could describe the Platform API, while a separate physical row described the available ChatGPT route.

Both paths now pass the catalog's physical routes to the existing auth planner through the same catalog view used by foreground runs. Dispatch reads the published catalog captured at admission. It keeps the existing model transport when no catalog route is available. No new route selector, config field, or stored state is added.

The isolated-session contract in #159246 is unchanged; its changes in this file concern the documented isolation boundary, not auth route selection.

## Evidence

- On baseline `0a687e8e01d`, both route-order cases fail through `runIsolatedCompletion` with `No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.`
- With this fix, both orders select the subscription route, display the Codex runtime, and dispatch to the isolated harness with the subscription profile. The harness returns text through the real completion entry point. A missing pinned profile does not dispatch.
- The focused completion and plugin-scope suites pass: 56 tests. These include utility-model overrides, CLI profile selection, quota rotation, cancellation, and authority lifetime controls.
- The final focused regression in `src/agents/isolated-completion-route.test.ts` passes both route orders. The agent-root TypeScript check and changed-source lint pass.

The original route-order regression uses a synthetic catalog and mocked dispatch. The additional adapter-boundary regression below covers native login and inference serialization without contacting ChatGPT.

## Adapter boundary proof

The permanent [plugin-owned adapter regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/408cc759db6741b58063d348a765d0ff1a2c347f/extensions/codex/isolated-completion.adapter.e2e.test.ts) drives the real `runIsolatedCompletion` and auth planner through the existing test-only SDK barrel into the real Codex harness/client and a [stdio JSON-RPC executable](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/408cc759db6741b58063d348a765d0ff1a2c347f/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-isolated-app-server.fixture.mjs). The [core-only test fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/408cc759db6741b58063d348a765d0ff1a2c347f/src/agents/isolated-completion.adapter.test-support.ts) keeps bundled plugin implementation files out of core TypeScript graphs.

- **Allowed:** ChatGPT route is second behind Platform. The scoped synthetic account reaches `account/login/start` exactly once, then `turn/start`; completion returns `Completed as synthetic-allowed-account`. [Redacted transcript](https://gist.github.com/obviyus/ba2dd960adfd458f96736bf39d459f12#file-allowed-json).
- **Nearest forbidden:** a stored OAuth account explicitly pinned against config declaring that profile API-key-only is rejected by real eligibility policy; **zero RPC messages**. [Transcript](https://gist.github.com/obviyus/ba2dd960adfd458f96736bf39d459f12#file-forbidden-json).
- **Revoked:** remove the allowed profile and revoke caller authority while the real model-materialization await is held; release it and observe rejection before any RPC, including login/inference. [Transcript](https://gist.github.com/obviyus/ba2dd960adfd458f96736bf39d459f12#file-revoked-json).

All three moved cases pass (23.8 s test time; 78.8 s including cold transformation). Core-agent and extension-test TypeScript checks and targeted lint pass. `check-changed` passes extension/core-import and SDK boundary checks, then stops only at the known UI E2E root budget (722/720). Merged current `origin/main`, including its managed-cleanup lint fix. Synthetic principals and isolated state only; no live ChatGPT request, real credentials, user Gateway, or default login. Admission/catalog inputs and the deferred model resolver are fixture-controlled; auth planning, profile scoping, native serialization, process transport, and result handling are real. No production execution changes. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Merge danger: two-way door. Reverting the patch fully restores the old behavior; it writes no state. The blast radius is auth planning for harness-owned isolated completions and their runtime labels when a model has multiple physical catalog routes.

feat(skills): Learned notice row with one-press Undo (#167996)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a background skill review's result shows in the Control UI as a large chat bubble that looks like an agent reply, and undoing it means typing "undo" and waiting for a model turn.

## User Impact

User impact:
- **Control UI:** the result is one quiet **Learned** line under the reply ("Learned · Updated `deploy-staging` · Created `release-notes`  Undo"). Each skill name opens that skill in the Skill Workshop, and **Undo** reverts the whole review in one press, then shows **Undone**.
- **Channels with buttons** (Telegram, Discord, Feishu, Teams, …): the notice carries a native **Undo** button. Plain-text channels show the copyable command `/learn undo <id>`.
- **Slack:** no notice is posted at all (owner decision). The change still appears in the Skill Workshop and can be undone there.
- Replying "undo" still works. Once a button undo has run, the agent is told, so a later chat "undo" does not revert twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One undo owner:** `undoWorkshopReview` (`src/skills/workshop/review-undo.ts`) reverts every skill one review changed. It restores the version saved before the review's first change of each skill, or archives a skill the review created. Reverts are recorded under `skill-workshop-undo:<id>`, so a repeated press finds them and reports `already-undone`. It skips a created skill that is already gone, for example after the agent undid it from chat. Concurrent presses are serialized. It refuses before any write if the change feed was pruned past the review's start (the feed keeps 500 rows) or if a saved version it needs is gone. If a later revert still fails, the error names the reverts that already committed, and the agent is told about them. When it reverts something, it queues a note for the reviewed session so the agent does not revert again.
- **Entry points, all on that owner:**
  - New Gateway method `skills.workshop.undo { agentId?, runId } -> { status, changes }`. It uses `operator.admin` and the same admission and authority recheck as `skills.workshop.restore`.
  - New `/learn undo <id>`, owner-only, the same gate as `/config set`. Only the exact `undo <uuid>` form is the subcommand; any other text stays a learn request.
  - The channel notice's Undo button is a shared-presentation `command` action, so no new channel code. The Telegram callback data is 54 of 64 bytes.
- **Control UI:** the notice is rendered in the Carapace turn-recap anatomy (`.oc-turn-recap`: hairline rules around one muted line). It uses sentence case, a lightbulb icon, skill names as quiet mono text buttons and one square ghost **Undo** with pending, done and error states. It follows the Carapace rules: square radii, no pills or cards, one action, theme tokens, and reduced-motion safe. The writer adds a typed marker to the transcript-only row (`kind: "skill-workshop-change"`, `agentId`, `runId`, `skills`). The text body stays for the TUI, search and older clients.
- The Skill Workshop page accepts `?skill=<name>` and opens that skill in whichever list holds it. A skill link first selects the notice's own agent through the app's agent selection, so a `main` notice never opens another agent's same-named skill.

fix(models): use the configured proxy for local catalog refresh (#168554)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models list --refresh` skips the configured managed proxy when no Gateway is running.

## User Impact

Users can refresh provider models through their configured proxy without starting a Gateway. Cached lists and Gateway requests still bypass CLI proxy startup. No config changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI startup policy bypasses the proxy for model lists. Local refresh can make provider requests after that decision. Start the existing managed proxy only around local refresh, and release it in `finally`, including when discovery fails.

## Evidence

- The regression test on main (`8bb392d9810`) failed in two cases: local refresh did not start the proxy, and failed discovery did not release its handle. With this change, all 24 tests in `list.prepared-catalog.test.ts` passed. These cases also cover cached lists and Gateway refresh without proxy startup.
- Ran the CLI with an isolated profile and no Gateway, using a local HTTP proxy and a synthetic Ollama server. The proxy logged `CONNECT 192.168.254.254:19875`, `GET /api/tags`, and `POST /api/show`. The CLI returned `ollama/proxy-proof:latest` as available, with a `ready` provider outcome.
- Targeted lint passed. The formatter ran on the changed test, and `git diff --check` passed. Full-repository checks were not run locally.
- The cached CLI command exited successfully with no proxy startup message and no new proxy log entries. It returned an empty cached inventory.

Merge risk: two-way door; a revert restores the prior behavior without a state migration. The change affects only provider discovery during local `models list --refresh`. Cached lists and Gateway transport keep their current policy.

feat(compaction): default to provider-native compaction on OpenAI and Anthropic API-key routes (#168164)

Related: #168070, #168088

## What Problem This Solves

Provider-native ("server-side") compaction keeps the full conversation in a provider checkpoint. It was available but mostly off:

- **OpenAI API key:** automatic compaction used `/responses/compact`, but a manual `/compact` always ran client-side summarization.
- **Anthropic API key:** threshold compaction was opt-in only.

Live runs also exposed three defects on these paths:

- **Paid result discarded silently.** `/responses/compact` stored the system prompt inside the returned window. When transcript redaction would change that window (for example, a session key `agent:apikey:…` matched a credential pattern), OpenClaw threw away the paid result, logged it only at DEBUG, and paid again for a client summary.
- **Rejected Anthropic checkpoint looped.** When Anthropic rejected a replayed compaction block, the "do not resend" marker lived only on an error output that is never persisted. Every later turn sent the same block and got another 400.
- **Anthropic summarizer could call a tool.** With tools defined, Anthropic's default summarizer can call a tool instead of summarizing (documented limitation).

## Fix

- **OpenAI API key** (`openai` / `openai-responses` / `api.openai.com`):
  - Manual `/compact` without focus text now uses `/responses/compact`, like automatic compaction. `/compact <focus>` and overflow recovery stay client-side. `params.responsesCompactEndpoint: false` disables it.
  - The system prompt is sent as the endpoint's `instructions` field ([API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/compact)), not inside `input`, so checkpoints no longer store it.
  - A redaction pre-check on the request content skips the paid call when the stored window could not be saved.
  - Every skip, discard and fallback logs a WARN with its reason.
- **Anthropic API key, direct `api.anthropic.com`:**
  - Threshold compaction is on by default for the models Anthropic documents for it. `params.anthropicServerCompaction: false` opts out; `true` still opts in other Claude models. OAuth/subscription, Bedrock, Vertex and proxies stay off.
  - Every compaction edit sends tool-free summarization `instructions`.
  - Null compaction blocks are not captured.
  - A rejected replayed block is durably stripped from its transcript owner, so the next turn sends full history.
- **Local preflight:** the default Anthropic trigger, `max(50k, 0.7 × budget)`, sits below local preflight compaction, so Anthropic compacts first. Only an explicit opt-in holds local preflight back to the trigger, as before.
- **Memory flush:** server compaction (Anthropic threshold and OpenAI inline) is always off for memory-flush runs, so memory extraction sees the unsummarized history.
- **Public API:** `@openclaw/ai/transports` keeps `OpenAIResponsesCompactionRejection` as a deprecated alias of `CompactionReplayRejection`, and `resolveOpenAIResponsesCompactEndpointPlan` still accepts its old third `purpose` argument (ignored).
- **Not in this PR:** ChatGPT sign-in (Codex-style remote compaction V2). It moved to #168088 after review showed the request has to be built by the normal-turn pipeline to keep the prompt cache. That route is unchanged here.

## User Impact

- **Anthropic API-key users** on Claude Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6+, and the 5.x models get provider compaction with no extra request. The next turn reads 88–89% of its input from cache, against 44% after client compaction.
- **OpenAI API-key users** get full-fidelity provider checkpoints from manual `/compact`. Next turns are smaller and 91% cached. Each manual `/compact` reads about 131k uncached input tokens, against about 7.4k for a client summary (measured below).
- **Opt-out:** `params.responsesCompactEndpoint: false` (OpenAI) or `params.anthropicServerCompaction: false` (Anthropic). Existing sessions keep working; checkpoints are fenced by provider, model, endpoint, auth profile and session.

## Evidence

### Live benchmark

Isolated Gateway, synthetic workspace corpus (measured before the ChatGPT code was split out; the API-key route has changed since only by an equivalent inline endpoint check), three facts planted by the user before compaction. Recall was checked on the first turn after compaction. The host was loaded (1-minute load 34–56 on 32 cores), so wall times are upper bounds.

**OpenAI API key, gpt-6-astra, ~140k-token session, manual `/compact`:**

| | Server (`/responses/compact`) | Client summary |
|---|---:|---:|
| Provider requests | 1 | 2 |
| Compaction input tokens | 130,642 / 131,186 (0 cached) | 7,461 / 7,422 (0 cached) |
| Compaction output tokens | 1,186 / 1,123 | 771 / 793 |
| Compaction wall time (CLI) | 23.3 s / 34.0 s | 18.1 s / 17.9 s |
| Checkpoint size | 14,264 / 13,176 encrypted chars | text summary |
| Tokens before → after | 130.6k → 17.9k / 131.2k → 17.6k | 140.2k → 13.8k / 140.3k → 13.8k |
| Next turn input, cached | 20.2k, 18.4k cached (91%) | 37.6k, 9.1k / 18.4k cached (24% / 49%) |
| Recall of planted facts | 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3, 3/3 |

**Anthropic API key, claude-sonnet-5-5, ~100k-token session, trigger lowered via `anthropicCompactThreshold`:**

| | Server (inside the turn) | Client summary (manual) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Extra provider requests | 0 | 2 |
| Compaction pass | 97.9k input (23.2k cache read, 74.5k cache write), ~830 output | 7.5k input, 1.6k output |
| Wall time | 10.4 s / 14.2 s for compaction plus the answer | 16.1 s |
| Next turn input, cache read | 24.1k / 24.4k, 21.4k read (88–89%) | 49.1k, 21.4k read (44%) |
| Recall of planted facts | 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3 |

**Before this fix (same OpenAI route):** a session key in the system prompt matched a redaction pattern. The paid `/responses/compact` result (130.7k input, ~18 s) was discarded at DEBUG, then 2 more client requests ran, about 37 s in total.

### Targeted live probes

- **Anthropic with a tool defined** (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-sonnet-5-5 with thinking): a summary is captured on every run. Replay shrinks the prompt from about 70–92k to about 1k tokens. Thinking blocks after the compaction block replay fine over 3 turns, with a cache read on turn 3. Seeded facts are recalled.

### Tests

- Every changed test file passes. Regressions fail on the pre-fix code:
  - redaction skip before fetch (endpoint not called);
  - `instructions` request body;
  - durable stripping of a rejected Anthropic checkpoint (real `streamAnthropic` with a SQLite session manager);
  - null-block capture;
  - default-on Anthropic keeps the local preflight threshold.
- `pnpm run tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` and `tsgo:test:packages` pass. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes.
- External review: five rounds of an independent model review. Every finding was resolved; the ChatGPT-specific findings moved to #168088.

session rotation), but its accounting fact carried no latch intent, so the
accounting-only keep default preserved byte-preflight suppression across
the rewrite and the next turn skipped byte compaction for changed host
history. Durable facts now mark a committed host compaction, and both
persistence consumers clear the latch on that mark while native-only

fix: retain updater preparation and service handoff timings (#168409)

## What Problem This Solves

Update reports omit the running updater's retained-runtime preparation and report no measured duration for native service reconciliation or the fresh-driver handoff. A long quiet interval can therefore look like candidate-state copying even when the old Gateway is still serving.

## User Impact

Operators can see `updater-runtime-retention` in the JSON result and bounded run history, including the existing inventory/materialization counts and durations. The native executor probe and successful install/restart child have separate timers. Fresh-driver finalization reports the interval from the previous driver's last completed receipt to resuming finalization.

The change reports time; it does not make updates faster or alter admission, stop, restart, recovery, or verification decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-up to #168290. In its single instrumented run, result steps totaled 811.368s against 1,875.067s overall. The largest residual is before the candidate snapshot: a 1,136.917s interval contains 289.982s of explicit Git/install/build steps, leaving 846.935s unallocated. The existing `updater-runtime-retention` progress timer never reached the returned result and could be evicted from history. Preserve that timer rather than introducing a new tracing format.

Read-only inspection found 145,186 regular files in that run's retained runtime. Retention inventories and hashes regular files before materialization, even when it can hardlink their bytes. This is a plausible large-cost owner, **not proof that retention alone consumed the 846.935s residual**. No new update run or optimization was performed. The old Gateway remained ready throughout this interval.

## Compatibility and Evidence

- Rebased the service/handoff change onto main after #168290 landed.
- Reuses `UpdateStepResult` and existing ledger timestamps. No schema, persisted record shape, timeout, or update policy change; the retention list changes eviction priority inside the existing byte/count limits.
- The installed updater owns retention and service timing, so those observations require the updated driver on a subsequent update. The fresh worker owns handoff timing and can report it on the installing hop using existing parent receipts.
- Focused proof covers service probe/child separation, preserved failure behavior, result-to-ledger propagation, fresh-driver receipt timing, retention result publication, bounded-history eviction and existing-row compatibility.
- No new live update was run. The published 2026.9.8-to-candidate and instrumented same-tree evidence in #168290 remains the live behavior boundary; these additional timers are covered by the focused regressions.
- Focused checks passed: 81 tests covering the service command, service lifecycle, fresh-driver worker, ledger compaction, CLI retention result, revoked-owner restart paths, and update/Doctor failure receipts. Focused source lint and formatting passed.
- Negative control on clean main `123d5a1331a`: the new retention-result assertion fails because the timer is missing from result steps, and all three bounded-history cases fail because retention timing is evicted. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- Failure-receipt tests preserve their strict step ordering with the new retention prefix. The worker ledger mock explicitly isolates real state, and its obsolete mock-baseline exception was removed.
- No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert removes additional diagnostic observations. Existing run rows remain readable. Blast radius is update-result diagnostics and their bounded history; service commands and update behavior are unchanged.

fix(models): Claude CLI models vanish from the picker after a plugin config change (#168315)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Claude CLI (`claude-cli/*`) model disappears from the model picker and `models.list` after a dynamic config change to `agents` or `plugins`, such as turning on ACP OpenCode in Models settings, until the catalog is explicitly refreshed.

## User Impact

User impact: Claude CLI models stay listed when another plugin or agent setting changes while the Gateway is running. Turning ACP OpenCode on now shows its models next to Claude CLI instead of replacing them.

## Why This Change Was Made

A config change to `agents` or `plugins` rebuilds the prepared model catalog. The rebuild keeps a discovered provider's rows only when the new agent facts prove the same account. Claude CLI availability comes from a discovery-only native sign-in credential that the rebuild's agent facts do not carry, so its rows were dropped. The follow-up changed-only pass then only looked at providers with stored credentials, so nothing reacquired Claude CLI.

The changed-only pass now also reacquires providers that the rebuild could not retain and that the new inventory still lacks. Retention rules are unchanged: unverifiable rows are still not carried over. The provider is reacquired under the new generation. The changed-only provider selection moved next to the retention decision in `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-source.ts`, which keeps `catalog-access.ts` under its line cap.

No config, schema, or protocol changes.

## Evidence

Regression: `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts` › "reacquires discovered providers that a config rebuild cannot retain". It publishes an inventory in which one provider's credential exists only in discovery auth, rebuilds after an unrelated `plugins` change, and runs the changed-only pass.
- origin/main production code: fails, catalog is `[ 'plain/plain-model' ]` (the discovery-only provider is gone, no worker reacquisition).
- This branch: passes.

Real Gateway (isolated loopback profile, native `claude` login, no API keys, acpx `nativeAgents.opencode=false` at start). `config.patch` set `plugins.entries.acpx.config.nativeAgents.opencode=true` (dynamic reload, no restart), then `models.list`:

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| origin/main a285e8b | claude-cli 11, kimi 4, openai 8 | acp-opencode 84, kimi 4, openai 8 (**claude-cli 0**) | acp-opencode 84 only |
| this branch | claude-cli 11, kimi 4, openai 8 | acp-opencode 84, claude-cli 11, kimi 4, openai 8 | acp-opencode 84 + claude-cli 10 |

Toggling it back off on this branch kept claude-cli 11 in every sample, and no sample returned an empty list. On main, a `refresh: true` before the toggle did not prevent the drop.

A Claude CLI turn (`openclaw agent`, session model `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5`) on the same Gateway went through the Claude Code CLI runner. Claude Code refused it at the account's usage cap with `{"type":"cli_error","message":"You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 12 …"}`. That confirms the routing, but there is no completed reply.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary Gateway downtime when updates run optional Doctor inspections while the service is stopped.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed updater advertises that it will finish the inspection pass after restart. Doctor defers only lint-backed, read-only checks. The finalizer runs those checks with explicit selectors and informational findings enabled, after verified readiness. An incomplete pass is advisory; uncertain child-process cleanup still propagates through the existing recovery boundary.

The capability is internal, not a new configuration option. Older installed updaters do not advertise it, so an upgrade from 2026.9.8 retains the original inspection behavior rather than losing diagnostics. `--no-restart`, unowned/stopped plugin-only services, and copied-state rehearsals retain their existing behavior.
