feat(models): show each provider's recommended models first in pickers (#167370)

## What Problem This Solves

Model pickers list every model a provider serves in catalog order, so the handful OpenClaw actually recommends are buried among older and niche models. The hosted catalog already carries each provider's `recommendedModels` (#166737), but no picker reads it.

## User Impact

In the Control UI chat and New Session pickers, each provider group shows Default, the current model, then that provider's recommended models in list order. Everything else sits behind a collapsed **All models (N)** row inside the group. Search still matches every model, and the disclosure is hidden while searching.

- Terminal `/models` lists the current model, every provider's recommended models, and all models of providers that recommend none, then an **All models (N)** row holding the rest. Enter on it reveals them in place. Typing a search matches every model.
- Text `/models <provider>` pages list the current model, then the recommended models, then the rest. They are already paged and end with `All: /models list <provider> all`, so they get the new order but no new structure.
- Providers with no recommendations, and installs without a downloaded v2 catalog, keep today's lists with no disclosure.
- Recommended ids that the provider no longer serves, or that the picker view hides, are skipped.

Channel button menus (Telegram/Discord interactive `/models`), settings model dropdowns and the CLI onboarding picker are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One ordering rule.** `orderModelCatalogForPicker`, the picker-order owner from #157869, now ranks each provider's rows by that provider's `recommendedModels` from the active hosted catalog, ahead of the provider-owned remainder. It keeps the selected model first. `models.list` and text `/models` both read through this owner, so every surface gets the same order.
- **One additive protocol field.** `models.list` rows (and the `models.snapshot` built from them) gain an optional `recommended: true`, set by the same ranking. Clients need it to know where the collapsed section starts. No version bump or capability: released clients ignore an unknown optional field, and the Control UI ships with its Gateway.
- **Surface rendering only.** The chat picker splits each group into lead and **All models** rows and reuses the provider-group toggle and DOM search (search ignores the disclosure). The TUI's searchable list gains generic collapsed rows plus an expander row.

No config, stored data or catalog publication changes.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateways (fresh state dirs, loopback ports, fake provider keys, a deny-all egress proxy) served a local copy of the production v2 catalog (1,048 models across 44 providers) through `models.catalogRefresh.url`. Base is `origin/main` at 8958390b8aa. The candidate is this branch. The same harness drove the real Control UI in Chromium and the real `openclaw tui` in tmux on both.

* fix(agents): sessions_send into a busy session is reported queued but never runs

A Gateway `agent` run into a session whose turn is still running was rejected
during admission with SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED: the running turn's own
restart-recovery fence made claimMainSessionRecoveryOwner return
`invalidated`. sessions_send reported `accepted`/`queued`, the pending input
went straight to `interrupted`, and asynchronous reply-backs and failure
notices into a busy requester were lost. chat.send into the same busy session

When the claim fails only because every fence belongs to a run of this
session that is still executing in the current lifecycle (it holds its
runtime handle or run context; it may hold its own delivery claim), the
command now waits for that run, bounded by its own timeout and abort signal,
then prepares and claims again under the unchanged rules. Recovery and
delivery debt of any other run, other generations, retained fences without a
live execution (for example after sessions_yield), the subagent
settle/announce terminal guard and stale-generation rejection keep failing as
before.

fix(plugin-sdk): block removal of shipped stable SDK surface without a dated compat record (#167036)

Related: #166404

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: shipped Plugin SDK subpaths and exports could be removed without the surface check noticing, which broke published third-party plugins such as `@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin` on 2026.10.1-beta.1.

## User Impact

User impact: the stable Plugin SDK surface can no longer silently disappear. Removing a subpath or named export that shipped in the latest stable release now fails `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` unless a compatibility record covers it with a final compatibility day that has passed. No runtime behavior changes; nothing is restored here (restoring the removed subpaths for #166404 is a separate product decision).

## Why This Change Was Made

`plugin-sdk:surface:check` only enforced maximum export-count budgets, and the API baseline diff is report-only. The commits that retired `config-runtime`, `infra-runtime`, `channel-message`, `command-auth` and four other subpaths (912+ named exports that shipped in v2026.9.8) lowered those budgets in the same change, so the check passed. A ceiling cannot detect a removal.

This adds a committed inventory of the latest stable release's typed public surface (`scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json`, pinned to the current npm `latest` v2026.9.9: 158 typed subpaths, 4,591 named exports, identical to v2026.9.8). It is generated from the release tag's package exports and declarations by `pnpm plugin-sdk:shipped-surface:gen -- --release <tag>`, reusing the existing tagged-revision renderer from `plugin-sdk:api:diff`, and is regenerated during stable closeout (documented in RELEASING.md). The surface check compares the current tree against it:

- A missing shipped subpath, or a missing name in a surviving subpath, needs a compat record whose `surfaces` names `openclaw/plugin-sdk/<subpath>` (whole subpath) or the qualified `openclaw/plugin-sdk/<subpath>.<Name>`. Bare names do not count.
- The record must be `deprecated`, `removal-pending`, or `removed` with a `removeAfter` strictly before the current UTC date (the date is the final compatibility day). A `removalGate` alone or a future date does not authorize; budgets play no role.
- Packaged private runtime facades without a `types` condition are excluded: they are not a declared contract.

To make current `main` pass without restoring anything, the already-landed removals are recorded honestly:

- Dated tombstones for the five subpaths retired under the Sept 30 owner decision (`removeAfter` 2026-09-30) and new tombstones for `command-auth`, `discord`, `telegram-account`, whose records were deleted in 0d530ea5 (`removeAfter` 2026-10-01).
- 14 later named-export removals from surviving subpaths (2fec39f5 #165431, bd64d93f #165288, f2de06b3 #163587) recorded retroactively per owner decision; each release note states the export was removed without a compatibility window.
- The Skill Workshop proposal-hook types removed by cfee8511 (#161057) already had a tombstone; its surfaces are now qualified and dated.

Release-note context: Plugin SDK authors get a migration-guide row for each of the 14 retroactively recorded exports in `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces.md`.

## Evidence

- Inventory generation from tag `v2026.9.8` (fc23bc86): 158 typed subpaths, 4,591 names; `config-runtime` 115, `infra-runtime` 583, `channel-message` 136, `command-auth` 78 names.
- Historical transition, guard + inventory overlaid on throwaway worktrees with `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_SDK_SURFACE_NOW=2026-10-01`: `e649be31^` shows only pre-existing gaps; `e649be31` additionally fails on exactly `channel-lifecycle` (23), `channel-message` (136), `channel-reply-pipeline` (12), `config-runtime` (115), `infra-runtime` (583) despite its lowered budgets.
- Final tree: `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` → `shipped Plugin SDK v2026.9.8: no unauthorized removals`. Reverting the tombstone dates re-reports all eight subpaths; pinning `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_SDK_SURFACE_NOW=2026-10-07` re-reports the eight Skill Workshop types (strict date semantics).
- The guard already caught a live regression during this PR: cfee8511 landed on main mid-review and the rebased check failed on its eight unqualified types until the record was fixed.
- Regenerated against v2026.9.9 (bcfc8881) after it went stable mid-review: zero subpaths or names added or dropped versus v2026.9.8; check still clean.
- PR wrapper inventory lists the new compat-record module (first CI run failed `eager-import-closure` / `pr-worktree-provision` on its absence).
- Focused tests (`--maxWorkers=1`): `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.test.ts` 20 passed (~2.2 s wall), `src/plugins/compat/registry.test.ts` 12 passed, `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` 11 passed / 1 Linux-only skip; all three ~11.7 s wall. Pure evaluator tests, no TS project boots, no timers.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: every lane passed except two inherited from `main`: the dead-export scan (`observePlacementAuthority`, already fixed on main by 017842386a7f) and core lint on three over-length files this PR does not touch. Direct oxlint on all changed `.ts`/`.mts` files is clean.

chore(catalog): curate recommended models (#167338)

## What Problem This Solves

The curated recommended-models list (`scripts/lib/recommended-models.json`) was seeded mechanically with every model that had any ranking signal (85 ids). That tail included superseded models (`gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `hy3`, `minimax-m2.7`, `mimo-v2.5*`), domain variants with no usage (`ling-3-flash-*`), previews and lite tiers, and a stealth model whose launch period has ended (`space-bunny-alpha`). Each provider's published `recommendedModels` includes every listed model it serves, so those showed up next to frontier models.

## Fix

A manual curation pass, down to 27 ids:

- **Frontier first:** models with a positive LMArena Agent Arena score, in Arena order (Claude Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, Kimi K3, Grok 4.7, …).
- **Vendor flagships** that keep each vendor's own provider populated: `mistral-large-4` (added), `glm-5.3-flash`, `minimax-m3`, `qwen3.8-27b`, `mimo-v2.6-pro`, `step-5-preview`.
- **What OpenClaw users actually run:** OpenRouter's top models for the OpenClaw app this month are cheap and free open models (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash, MiniMax M3, Nemotron 3 Ultra/Super, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.3). They stay, and `deepseek-v4-flash` is re-added right after `deepseek-v4.1-flash` so hosts that serve only V4 still recommend it (where both are served, the newer one hides the older).
- `claude-haiku-5.5` stays, placed after `gpt-6-luna` so it doesn't push GPT-6.1 Sol out of aggregators' first five.

Supersedes #166789: its only change, adding `mistral-large-4`, is included here.

Maintainer decision (Ayaan): list contents curated manually. This pass deliberately drops older generations (`gpt-5.6-*`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `claude-haiku-4.5`, `gpt-oss-*`, `gemma-4-*`, …) even where a provider serves only the predecessor, so those providers get a shorter list (or none) instead of an older model. fix(models): one failed provider discovery hides its models until a manual refresh (#167230)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a provider's model discovery fails once (for example an OpenRouter timeout), the Gateway falls back to that provider's few built-in rows (OpenRouter 466 → 3) and keeps them until someone runs an explicit `models refresh`.

## User Impact

A transient provider outage no longer hides most of that provider's models for the life of the Gateway. The failed provider retries discovery in the background and its full model list comes back on its own once the provider is reachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Failed discovery recorded no renewal deadline, and ordinary `models.list` reads intentionally no longer renew inventory (#167008), so nothing ever retried it. A failed provider now gets a backed-off retry deadline (30 s, doubling to a 30 min cap) on its retained inventory facts. The catalog owner keeps one timer for the earliest deadline, re-armed after each acquisition settles and cancelled when the catalog generation retires. Reads stay passive; a successful retry publishes the full rows and returns the provider to its normal cache deadline. A compatible reload keeps the failure facts and resumes the retry.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts`: discovery fails, then recovers with backoff and no read or refresh (fails on `main`: the worker is never called again); and a new failure episode is measured from its own failure.

fix(models): adopting a downloaded catalog briefly hides discovered models (#167178)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the model picker and `models.list` drop every discovered model (for example all OpenRouter rows) while a running Gateway adopts a newly downloaded hosted catalog. If that provider's discovery then fails, the provider stays reduced to its built-in rows until someone runs an explicit refresh.

A production Gateway showed this during a fleet catalog refresh: the list fell from 599 to 54 models for about 2.5 to 4 minutes.

## User Impact

While a Gateway adopts a new catalog, pickers and `models.list` keep showing the current models and prices. The new catalog's models and prices appear together, once its discovery has finished. Adoption itself now takes as long as that discovery (seconds in practice). The previous catalog keeps serving during that time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adoption (#158000) built each replacement owner with static rows only and published it. It then started that owner's discovery fire-and-forget. Readers therefore saw only configured and catalog rows until discovery finished. A failed discovery left them that way, because failed providers carry no renewal deadline.

Adoption now waits for each candidate's own discovery, inside the candidate's catalog scope, before the single commit. The wait can be cancelled through the adoption's existing abort signal. The post-commit fire-and-forget is removed. `loadFullModelCatalog` gets a `wait` option, so adoption awaits the acquisition instead of the 5 s foreground race that ordinary readers use. Rows and prices still switch in one commit, and admitted runs keep their captured pair (#140086).

Maintainer decision (Ayaan, delegated): adoption waits for candidate discovery. The previous catalog's rows and prices keep serving coherently in the meantime, which is strictly safer than publishing a partial list.

Maintainer decision (Ayaan, delegated): if a provider's discovery fails during adoption, that provider publishes with the new catalog's built-in rows. Rows are never carried across catalog versions (#140086). On `main` this is also the end state, but only after a window in which every discovered row was gone.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Regression test `keeps discovered rows published until the adopted catalog's discovery completes` holds the candidate's discovery and drives the real `models.list` handler. While discovery is held, readers still see the old catalog's discovered row and the old pricing generation. After release, they see only the new catalog's row and generation. It fails on `main` (`expected [ 'remote-200' ] to include 'discovered-200'`) and passes with this change. The existing "bounds refresh with two agents…" test now asserts that adoption publishes only after the held discovery completes. All 10 tests in `prepared-model-runtime.remote-publication.test.ts` pass, and `pnpm check:changed` is green.

Live, on an isolated Gateway (loopback, separate state):
- A local catalog mirror serves a fresh bundle per step. Each version renames `kimi/k3` to `Kimi K3 vN` and sets the input price of `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` to N $/M.
- OpenRouter's DNS resolution is delayed through a Node preload.
- `models.list` is polled every 50 ms.
- Adoption is triggered with `openclaw models refresh` followed by a `models.list` refresh.

| Adoption | `main` (adoption code unchanged on current `main`) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm (no delay) | 514 → **1** row (configured only) for 0.74–0.79 s, then 514 with the new marker | 514 rows throughout; marker switches 3.3 s after the trigger |
| Candidate discovery delayed 3–4 s (its own DNS lookup) | 514 → **1** row for 5.36 s | 514 rows throughout; marker switches 4.98 s and 5.42 s after the trigger, right after the candidate's lookup completes |
| Candidate discovery fails (60 s DNS, 5 s fetch timeout) | 514 → **1** row for 5.38 s, then 51 (OpenRouter 466 → 3 built-in rows) | 514 rows with the old marker for 7.2 s, then 51 with the new marker (decision above) |

On the final diff (rebuilt), the result was the same: a warm adoption with 994 rows throughout switched 2.1 s after the trigger. A 3 s delayed candidate discovery kept 994 rows throughout and switched 5.4 s after the trigger.

Prices follow the same commit. Usage for real `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` turns was computed at the bundled $0.75/M input before the marked catalogs. After adopting v28, v29 and v32, it was computed at exactly $28/$56, $29/$58 and $32/$64 per M (input/output). Real cheap turns (`openclaw agent … --model openai/gpt-5.4-mini`) completed with reply `ok` after each adoption. One turn on the final build hit a retryable agent-database admission error from the session-state layer, about 30 s after adoption. It is unrelated to the catalog, and the immediate retry succeeded.

Local review: `codex review --base origin/main` (model gpt-6-astra), round 1: "No actionable defects were found."

Merge danger: a two-way door. No stored state, schema, config or protocol changes, so a revert fully restores the previous behavior. Blast radius: every Gateway that adopts a downloaded hosted catalog. If this is wrong, adoption could stall behind a hung provider discovery. That wait is still bounded by each provider's own discovery timeouts and is cancelled by supersession, config reload or shutdown. Meanwhile the previous catalog keeps serving.

fix(models): reloading one provider's config hides models from unrelated discovered providers (#167117)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: changing any `models.*` config (for example an `openai` model entry) permanently removes the model rows of providers that were only found by full discovery, such as `claude-cli` and `kimi`. They stay missing from `models.list` and the model pickers until someone runs an explicit catalog refresh.

## User Impact

An unrelated config edit no longer hides discovered providers' models. A provider whose own config, plugin or credentials changed is still invalidated and rediscovered, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a reload, the catalog owner kept previous discovery only for configured or credentialed providers. Providers that full discovery found on its own were dropped, and the follow-up changed-only refresh only covers credentialed providers, so nothing brought them back. Retention now applies the same per-provider identity check (plugin fingerprint, provider config source, provider auth) to every provider in the previous inventory.

## Evidence

- Regression: the existing "invalidates retained discovery after the %s identity changes" test now also serves an unconfigured, uncredentialed provider. On `main` the endpoint and credential variants fail because its rows disappear; with this change they pass, the changed provider's rows are still dropped, and a plugin change still drops everything. `prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts`: 19/19 pass.
- Related suites (`prepared-model-runtime*.test.ts`, `prepared-model-catalog*.test.ts`): 322/323 passed in one loaded run. The remaining failure was a 10 s timeout in `prepared-model-catalog-worker.scope.integration.test.ts`; that file passes 5/5 on its own.
- Live, isolated Gateway (514 rows: openai 33, claude-cli 11, kimi 4, openrouter 466). I edited only `models.providers.openai` and polled `models.list` for 65 s:
  - `main`: 514 → 467 → 499. `claude-cli` and `kimi` never returned.
  - This branch: 514 → 482 (only `openai` briefly reloading) → 514 within about 1.4 s, and it stayed at 514.
- Review: local Codex review (gpt-6-astra) against `origin/main`, round 1: no findings.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. It is in-memory catalog retention only: no schema, stored-state or protocol change, and a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: Gateway model catalogs after config hot reloads. The risk is keeping a discovered provider's rows when that provider's identity changed in a way the existing source/auth/plugin fingerprint does not capture. That is the same check that already guards configured providers.

fix(update): repair turns time out before running tools (#166847)

* fix(update): stop repair turns timing out on per-check database copies

Delegated update repair turns handed their full authority assertion to the
embedded run as its source check. The run re-checks its source at every
preparation and tool boundary (~140 times per turn), and each check copied
the shared state database twice in synchronous snapshot children (~220 ms
each): once for the update-run row and once more because the requester's
nested current-authority scope discarded the enclosing fresh snapshot. On
clean main the checks consumed 59.4 s of a 65.6 s turn and the turn timed
out before any tool ran.

The turn now carries the run row and requester policy observed immediately
before it starts; settlement observes both again and refuses a revoked
result. In-turn checks verify the live executor fence, parent connection,
and cancellation. A nested current-authority snapshot for the same database
joins its enclosing fresh scope, restoring one copy per fresh check.

Same e2e tests, same Mac: (turn, validating) 65.6 s fail -> 7.1 s pass;
(turn, verifying) 56.5 s -> 7.4 s; fresh checks 142 -> 3.

* fix(update): keep requester authority live at repair tool admission

The previous revision handed the turn's cheap liveness check to tool
admission too, so a requester whose owner permission was removed while
inference awaited could still reach the next write or exec; settlement
refused the result only after the effect.

Repair turns now take two predicates. `isCurrent` remains the full fresh
authority (update-run row, requester policy, executor fence) and guards
each model candidate and, through the tool budget's new admission
predicate, each tool call at its last synchronous boundary. The optional
`isLive` serves the repeated run-admission and exec-guard checks; other
callers keep a single predicate.

A built-worker E2E case revokes the owner mid-inference and returns an
exec call: no marker is written and the turn reports requester-revoked.
It fails on the previous revision.

* docs(update): describe repair-turn authority checks at each effect

* fix(update): keep repair tool effect guards on full authority

Tool effect guards (pre-write and pre-spawn checks captured by
captureAgentToolSourceExecutionGuard) read the tool budget's scope
predicate, which the previous revision pointed at the cheap liveness
check. A requester revoked during a tool's own awaits could therefore
still reach the final write or spawn.

The tool budget again uses the full repair authority for admission and
every effect guard, as before this branch; only the prepared run-admission
source, which dominated the per-turn check count, uses `isLive`. The
budget's separate admission predicate is no longer needed and is removed.

A runtime test admits a tool, passes its effect guard, revokes the full
authority while liveness stays current, and expects the guard to refuse;
it fails when the budget uses the liveness check.

outside the source workspace keep their spelling, so a workspace whose

fix(agents): Astra answer lost when sessions_yield waits on its own async tools (#166876)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with GPT-6 Astra async tools, the model's real answer was lost when it called `sessions_yield` to wait for its own parallel tool results. Telegram received only a short follow-up "supplement", never the answer itself.

On our setup (Telegram forum topic, `openai/gpt-6-astra`, built-in runtime), one response ran `memory_search`, `exec` and `read` in parallel. It then wrote commentary plus `sessions_yield` ("Await source rows exec + memory recall + planning ref read"), and then, still in the same response, a 2,967-character `final_answer` checklist. The model wrote that checklist before seeing any tool result. A second model call (no new user input) saw the results and wrote a 332-character note: "One additional booking to check…". Only the note was sent.

## User Impact

When Astra waits for its own async tool results with `sessions_yield`, the response now really pauses. The model sees the results first and writes one complete answer. There are no new messages, notices or settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model's wait tool was not allowed to wait.

- #138046 (`a637374e435`) added Astra async tools and marks **every** function tool `async: true` (`openai-responses-client.ts`, `prepareRequest`), including `sessions_yield`. OpenAI's [async tool guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/async-tool-calling#add-a-wait-tool) says a wait tool must be an ordinary synchronous function: a sync call pauses the response, and the next request delivers the async results before the wait status. Because `sessions_yield` was async, Astra kept generating after the yield and answered without the results.
- The `sessions_yield` deferral (`hasUnobservedAsyncToolResults`, from #146667 `2f663805b4c`, reworded as `deferred` in #149983 `e252366ffe2`) was **not** spurious. The results were already in the transcript, but async results only reach the model in the next request, so the model had not seen them. The gate correctly keeps the yield from ending the turn. Its old text ("Finish this response to receive them") could never help, because the model only reads it in that next request.

The fix, at the owners:
- `Tool.async?: false` (llm-core) lets a tool opt out of async calls. The Responses transport keeps such tools synchronous and still marks every other function tool async. The two session tool projections that pick fields (`projectAgentToolDefinition`, `wrapToolDefinition`) carry the flag next to `executionMode`. The closed worker tool-surface schema (`WorkerToolSurfaceSchema`) accepts it, so worker-environment turns that carry `sessions_yield` still start.
- `sessions_yield` sets `async: false`. Its deferral now says what is true for a synchronous yield: the earlier results arrive with this result.
- `async: false` is documented as a supported tool property in `docs/plugins/tool-plugins.md`, next to `executionMode`, `hideFromChannelProgress` and `catalogMode`. Plugins can already reach it through `api.registerTool`. Other providers, Code Mode and Tool Search catalog calls are unchanged.

Maintainer decision (API direction): `async: false` is accepted as a supported, additive tool property. Scope: it keeps a directly visible function tool synchronous on GPT-6 Astra async-tool requests. Other providers, Code Mode and Tool Search catalog calls are unchanged. We chose this over a private carrier because the field is already reachable through `api.registerTool`, and a second private path (a transport option listing synchronous tool names) would add more code across agent-core stream options and the worker native runtime.

Kept from earlier decisions: the deferral gate and its non-error `deferred` status (#146667, #149983), and async execution for every other direct tool (#138046). Code Mode and non-Astra routes are untouched. Not changed: other ways the model might wait, such as `process` polling.

Boundaries a `sessions_yield` definition crosses on its way to an Astra async-tool request: the local and sub-agent session projections (both carry the flag), the shared `prepareRequest` (used by SSE, WebSocket, steering continuation, and compaction or retry rebuilds), and the worker tool surface (schema fixed here; the worker side spreads the definition). The native worker runtime passes `context.tools` through unchanged. Gateway-placed worker inference copies only name, description and parameters, but that path never enables async tool execution, so no tool is async there. Ordinary local turns do not cross the worker surface; its only producer is `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-execution.ts:358`.

## Evidence

**Regressions**
- `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-client.continuation.test.ts`: the real `createSessionsYieldTool` and a plain tool go through the real session projections (`toToolDefinitions` → `wrapToolDefinition`) into the real Responses transport for `gpt-6-astra` with async tools on. The test asserts `exec` is sent `async: true` and `sessions_yield` is not. With the transport fix reverted it **fails** (`sessions_yield` is sent with `"async": true`). On this branch it passes (47 tests).
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-gateway-tool-runtime.test.ts`: the gateway issues the real `sessions_yield` through `getSurface`, and the surface must validate and keep `async: false`. With the schema line reverted it **fails** with `Worker tool surface is invalid` (the round-1 review blocker: worker turns could not start).
- Also green on the final code: `prepared-tool-surface`, `agent-tool-definition-adapter*`, `tool-definition-wrapper`, `worker.runtime`, `worker-gateway-tools`, `worker-turn-rpc`, `sessions-yield-tool` (11 files, 230 tests), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt/oxlint on changed files, `docs:check-links`, `docs:check-mdx`, `git diff --check`.

**Live: Telegram Test Server with real `gpt-6-astra`.** Each run used its own forum topic and an isolated gateway on built `dist` (state under `/tmp`). The config matches our setup: the official `https://api.openai.com/v1` endpoint (async tools on), built-in runtime, code mode off, tool search on, `streaming.progress` with tool progress and commentary, thinking `low`. After the round-1 fix the build was `08acaf0afac`, which has the same code as this head (only `docs/plugins/tool-plugins.md` changed since). Message ids are the userbot's.

Incident shape (a). Same prompt both sides: a rough card list, then "start both checks together: cat card-export.csv with exec and open trip-notes.md with the read tool, and call sessions_yield to wait for them. Don't hold the checklist for the files: right after the sessions_yield call, write the dated checklist from my list; when the results arrive, add only what they change." The files hold two facts the list lacks: the hotel was personal, and one dinner was split four ways.

| Response 2 | "Two corrections from the files: …" | the full checklist plus "File-check changes: Hotel: exclude … Jalan Alor: four ways, ₹1,102.50 each …" |
| Model requests | 2 | 2 |
| Bot messages (userbot view) | 1: msg 39, "Two corrections from the files: …". **The checklist never arrived.** | 1: msg 90, "Splitwise checklist — 8 October 2026 / From your rough list … File-check changes … Final shared total: ₹88,944 …" |

Both sides also posted a progress draft (`Working / Exec / Read…`), which was deleted when the answer landed.

On (d): every live `NO_REPLY` shape we tried reached a reply contract that requires visible text, and this PR changes none of that code. A direct user request in a group is a required-reply turn. After a yield, the requester's completion wake must produce a visible final ("A yield owes the conversation a visible final unless private findings let the requester choose silence", `subagent-announce.requester-settle-state.ts:170-172`). The three completion-wake runs showed the same retry (`empty response detected … visible-answer continuation`). Ambient room events never reached the model. The user-request case matches `origin/main` exactly.

(f) worker-placed turn: our setup has no worker environments, so ordinary turns never cross the worker surface. The worker regression above covers it.

- Runtime: one `Set` built from the request's tool list, only on Astra async-tool requests. No new requests, timers, state, settings or messages. A yield that waits for async results no longer produces a blind answer, so the incident case saves one wasted answer of about 400 output tokens.

That is $3.59 for exploration and the first before/after pair, and $4.97 for the final-head siblings and the `origin/main` `NO_REPLY` baseline. fix(build): serialize unified tsdown runtime bundles to cap peak memory (#157739)

Closes #157782
Related: #157783 (declaration-stage memory; not addressed here)

## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm build` thrashes or is OOM-killed on hosts with about 10GB of memory during the `tsdown-unified` step. Since the unified group emits one tsdown config per bundled plugin (#144252), that runtime-only invocation admits all configs at once. The memory that grows is Rolldown's native allocation, so `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` cannot bound it.

## Fix

`scripts/tsdown-build.mts` already honors an explicit `--concurrency`. The `tsdown-unified` step in `scripts/build-all.mts` now passes `--concurrency 1`. Same output, serial admission; each bundle keeps its internal parallelism.

## User Impact

The `tsdown-unified` step peaks at roughly half its previous memory, at the cost of a few seconds of extra step time. This does not by itself make a full cold build fit 10GB: native declaration compilers still peak higher and are tracked separately (#157783).

## Evidence

Contributor measurements (Ubuntu 26.04, Node 24.21.0, per-process RSS sampled every 2s during `pnpm build`):

| Checkout | `tsdown-unified` peak RSS | step time |
|---|---|---|
| main `0963fd5da97`, defaults | 9.2GB / 9.5GB (two runs) | 32–35s |
| main, `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352` | 9.5GB | 35s |
| `ef9be3d8cfa` (before per-plugin configs) | 4.6GB | 19s |
| this branch (`--concurrency 1`) | 4.5GB | 50s |

Maintainer re-measurement on a Linux 32-vCPU builder (Node 24.21.0, tsdown 0.23.0, Rolldown 1.2.9), three runs each:

| Runtime policy | Median process-tree RSS | Median elapsed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default | 10.86GiB | 28.6s |
| `--concurrency 1` | 6.11GiB | 34.0s |

- All 14,293 runtime output paths matched by hash, mode and symlink target across default/1/2/4 runs.
- Tracing observed 46 simultaneously admitted configs by default and 1 with this change.
- Full `pnpm build` from a clean `dist` completes on this branch.

chore(models): daily report suggesting recommended-models list changes (#166738)

Builds on #166737 (merged: curated `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json` + shared `canonicalModelKey`/`canonicalModelFamily`/`compareModelRecency`); this PR only adds the helper script and its test.

## What Problem This Solves

The recommended-models list is now curated by hand, so a maintainer needs a daily, reviewable signal for what to change: new releases, Arena reorderings, and entries that are retired or no longer served.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Maintainers (and later a daily draft-PR agent) can run

```
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/suggest-recommended-models.mts [--list <path>]
```

and get a markdown report ending in a unified diff against `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json`. The list file is never written; a human edits it.

## Why This Change Was Made

TypeScript port of the recv2 prototype's ranking: LMArena Agent Arena score first; equal scores, and models without one, order by OpenRouter 30-day usage. The newest served family member without its own Arena row takes the slot of its newest ranked older sibling, counting at least that sibling's usage, so it sorts directly ahead of it (release date decides recency, so grok-4.20 does not outrank grok-4.7). DeepSWE is dropped; `-fast` and other serving variants fold into the base model.

- Inputs: every run fetches each source fresh, with no cache; a failed request or a response that fails schema validation fails that run. Sources: LMArena Agent Arena `agent/latest` through the HF datasets-server JSON rows endpoint (no parquet dependency), OpenRouter `/api/v1/models`, OpenRouter `rankings-daily` (only when `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set; otherwise curated entries without an Arena score keep their order), Vercel `/v1/models`, and the hosted catalog v2.
- Identity: each source id resolves once through the shared `canonicalModelKey`, with its display name, so dated aliases join their versioned model. Examples: `mistral-small-2603` is Mistral Small 4, OpenRouter `mistral-large-4-0` matches Vercel `mistral-large-4`, and usage arrives through OpenRouter `canonical_slug`. Non-chat models are excluded by gateway modality or type labels; `-latest` aliases are excluded.
- Report sections:
  - **New models:** first seen within 7 days and not listed. Each shows its likely same-family predecessor and both prices, and is flagged `possible new class` when either price differs by more than 2x or the family has no predecessor.
  - **Arena moves:** rank changes among entries both lists keep, largest first.
  - **Gone or deprecated:** first-party retired with its replacement, no longer served, or no signal.
  - **Suggested list:** the full ordered list plus the diff.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes (the PR adds one new file).

## Evidence

- Port fidelity: on the live inputs, the helper reproduced the prototype's 86-id suggested list exactly before the review-driven identity fixes. Two differences remain, and #166737's seed list already includes both: `mistral-medium-2604` is folded into `mistral-medium-3.5` because they are the same model, and `ling-3.0-flash-*` is now spelled `ling-3-flash-*` because zero minor versions fold.
- Typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json` and `tsgo:test:root` report no errors; scoped oxlint and oxfmt are clean. `canonical-model-key.test.ts` passed 32/32.
- Ordering: `test/scripts/suggest-recommended-models.test.ts` feeds stubbed sources through the real entry point. Two models tied on Arena score order by usage (the higher-usage one first, against alphabetical order), and a successor that inherits its sibling's Arena slot still sorts ahead of that higher-usage sibling. With the previous alphabetical tiebreak the test fails.
- Cost: `pnpm test test/scripts/suggest-recommended-models.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 2.2 s wall end to end (Vitest 0.78 s; the test itself 9 ms). CI on this head: run 37692398322, green in 595 s wall and 5,717 job-seconds across 58 jobs for the whole PR; the new test adds about 9 ms of that.
- Error and fallback paths: a list containing `claude-opus-4.8` reported "retired by its first-party provider; replaced by claude-opus-5", and `nonexistent-model-9` reported "no host serves it". A missing `--list` file exits 1 with a clear message. Without a key, the report states that usage was skipped and keeps unscored curated entries. With an invalid `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, the run exits 1 with `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/datasets/rankings-daily returned HTTP 401` and prints no report.
- Live run: all inputs were fetched fresh (5 requests, 3.9 s wall). Both outputs below are copied verbatim. In the live data the only exact Arena ties are successor/sibling pairs (`gpt-5.6`/`gpt-5.4`, `mimo-v2.6-pro`/`mimo-v2.5-pro`), and each successor sorts first.

fix(sessions): keep synchronous generation reads available during identity-preserving publications (#166758)

While any publication on a session row was pending, synchronous generation reads
(delivery, subagent control, cron roots, memory audiences) treated the session's
sessionId and lifecycleRevision as unknown and failed closed, even for metadata
writes that cannot change them. Long agent turns write their own row
constantly, so a memory plugin's synchronous currency check between its own
awaits intermittently failed with "memory audience currency is unavailable".

Committed publications now carry generationUnchangedKeys, proved from the
committed previous and current rows; synchronous generation reads ignore pending
publications that prove the session's incarnation unchanged. Prepared reads
still join every pending publication, so owners that order effects after a
session's in-flight write (subagent cancellation, provider readiness) are
unchanged. Created, deleted, archived, and membership-invalidated rows carry no
proof, and publication paths that do not supply it keep the existing fence. The
prepared-change record registry and its readers move beside the other
publication state to keep the publication owner within its line cap.

feat(catalog): publish curated recommended models per provider in catalog v2 (#166737)

## What Problem This Solves

The hosted catalog has no maintained notion of which models OpenClaw recommends. The only mechanism is a reserved per-provider `recommendedModels` field that each plugin manifest would have to author separately, and no manifest uses it.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. Pickers do not read the field. From now on, catalog v2 carries each provider's recommended models, taken from one hand-curated global list that maintainers review in PRs.

- Released clients (2026.9.7, 2026.9.8, 2026.10.1 betas) accept the new v2 output unchanged; see Evidence.
- Catalog v1 output is unchanged.
- Plugin manifests no longer author `modelCatalog.providers.<id>.recommendedModels` (shipped in 2026.9.7, never used). Manifests that still set it keep loading at runtime and at catalog publication; the field is ignored and never published. Tests cover both paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One list.** `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json` is an ordered array of canonical model ids (lowercase, vendor-less, dotted versions, no dates or serving variants), seeded with today's suggestion run (85 ids). The catalog generator already reads its other inputs from this repo, and the openclaw/catalog job runs that generator against `main` every four hours. A merged list edit therefore publishes on the next run, with no change to the catalog repo.
- **Per-provider projection.** At publication, the generator matches each provider's served model ids (and display names, for date-only ids such as Mistral's `mistral-medium-2604`) against the list through one shared `canonicalModelKey`/`canonicalModelFamily` module in `@openclaw/model-catalog-core`. Deprecated, disabled, and replaced rows stay in the catalog but never match, so a retired alias cannot win and a retired newer model cannot hide its served predecessor. Matches go into the existing per-provider v2 field, in list order and under the provider's own ids. When a provider serves several listed models of one family, only the newest appears.
- **Why per-provider, not top-level.** Released v2 readers reject unknown top-level keys, so a top-level field would stop catalog refresh for every released client. They already accept the per-provider field, so no reader change is needed.
- **Fail closed.** Publication fails, leaving the previous hosted catalog in place, when a list entry is not canonical, appears twice, or the list exceeds 200 entries.
- **Docs.** The new [Recommended models](docs/concepts/recommended-models.md) page records the review rules: family = name minus version; a successor replaces its predecessor including on launch day; new classes need a reviewer's call; `-fast` variants fold into the base model; when to drop an entry; order by Arena agent score, then usage, with human override.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes: the only hit is `docs/docs.json` (#162255, Agents API guide), and this PR only adds one nav entry.

fix(openrouter): thinking levels collapse to "off, ultra" on a cold process (#166705)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenRouter models offer only `off, ultra` on a fresh process, so `openclaw agent --local` (and a Gateway's first turn) rejects valid levels such as `--thinking low` and silently turns a configured `thinkingDefault: max` into `off`.

## User Impact

User impact: configured OpenRouter models get their real thinking levels on the first turn of every process. `openai/gpt-5` offers minimal–high (no off, since reasoning is mandatory), `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` offers off/on, `deepseek/deepseek-r1` is always on, and a configured `max` on gpt-5 sends `high` instead of `minimal`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter thinking policy and dynamic model row read model capabilities from process memory only. That is deliberate (#160651, #166528): those reads run on synchronous session paths and must not touch SQLite or the network. On a cold process nothing has loaded yet when the prepared model runtime completes configured OpenRouter refs, so the row says `reasoning: false` and the level is chosen from that. Capabilities only load later, in `prepareDynamicModel`, after the level is fixed.

The static catalog build already runs asynchronously before that completion, and only for providers whose configured refs need it. Core now passes that selected scope (`providerIds`, an existing catalog-context field) into static catalog hooks, and OpenRouter's static hook awaits its capability loader when OpenRouter is selected: a worker read of the persisted catalog, or one fetch when nothing is persisted yet. Unscoped static runs (doctor validation, the catalog worker, the bundled static fallback) pass no scope and stay network-free. The synchronous reads are unchanged. The provider SDK catalog docs describe the scoped static run.

## Evidence

Live, real OpenRouter key, fresh isolated state per run, `openclaw agent --local`, request bodies captured at the HTTP client:

| Model / input | main (630e9697ed2) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-5 `--thinking low` | rejected: `Use one of: off, ultra` | `reasoning: {effort: "low"}` |
| gpt-5 `--thinking low` after a successful turn (SQLite populated) | rejected: `off, ultra` | `effort: "low"` |
| gpt-5 default | `effort: "minimal"` (off clamped) | `effort: "medium"` |
| gpt-5 `thinkingDefault: max` | `effort: "minimal"` | `effort: "high"` |
| gpt-5 `--thinking off` | accepted | rejected: `Use one of: minimal, low, medium, high, ultra` |
| claude-sonnet-4.5 `--thinking low` | rejected: `off, ultra` | `reasoning: {enabled: true}` |
| claude-sonnet-4.5 default | `enabled: false` | `enabled: true` |
| claude-sonnet-4.5 `--thinking off` | `enabled: false` | `enabled: false` |
| deepseek-r1 `--thinking low` | rejected: `off, ultra` | `enabled: true` |
| deepseek-r1 `--thinking off` | accepted (`enabled: true` sent) | rejected: `Use one of: always on, ultra` |

The claude-sonnet-4.5 default change (`enabled: false` → `enabled: true`) is the cold path now matching warm behavior on main. OpenRouter reports this model as `{mandatory: false}` with no default, and OpenClaw applies its existing default for reasoning-capable models. A main Gateway (f1862732145, isolated, claude-sonnet-4.5 configured, no `--thinking`) sends `enabled: false` on turn 1, then `enabled: true` on turns 2 and 3.

Gateway (isolated state and port, gpt-5 configured): first turn with `--thinking low` was rejected with `off, ultra` on main and sends `effort: "low"` with this PR; later turns were already correct on main.

Tests: new `extensions/openrouter/static-catalog.test.ts` fails on main (row stays `reasoning: false`) and passes here; it also checks that unscoped static runs make no request. Existing OpenRouter, capability-cache, provider-discovery and implicit-catalog suites pass.

Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local): `extensions/openrouter/static-catalog.test.ts` 23s wall (Vitest 15.9s, test body 19ms); `src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.discovery-scope.test.ts` 24s wall (Vitest 17.5s, 20 tests). Both are mostly transform time. Hosted CI run 37671257993 on 1f582feb218 passed all 79 jobs in 10m52s; the run does not report time per file.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. No stored data, config or schema changes; reverting restores the previous cold behavior. Blast radius: OpenRouter users (first turn may now wait for one catalog read or fetch before selection, which the turn already did later), plus any static catalog hook that starts reading the new optional `providerIds` (none besides OpenRouter today).

fix(catalog): hosted model catalog stops updating once models.dev exceeds 5 MiB (#166699)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the hosted model catalog (catalog.openclaw.ai) has not updated since 2026-09-29 because every scheduled publish fails with `models.dev response exceeds 5242880 bytes`. The models.dev feed grew to 5,342,076 bytes, 1.9% over the 5 MiB response cap; 48 consecutive Publish runs have failed since the last success, so Gateways keep refreshing a catalog frozen at 1,039 models.

## User Impact

User impact: the next scheduled catalog publish succeeds again, so `openclaw models refresh` and background catalog refreshes pick up models, metadata and prices added upstream since 2026-09-29. No client or published-schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 5 MiB cap was introduced for the pricing feeds (#113660); models.dev metadata hydration (#137131) started sharing it. models.dev publishes every provider's metadata in one document, so it now gets its own 32 MiB bound (about 6x today's size) while the other feeds keep 5 MiB (largest today: LiteLLM at 3.1 MB). The streamed byte check, early cancellation and error message are unchanged, and models.dev stays required: a failed fetch still aborts the publish rather than shipping a partial catalog.

## Evidence

- Real upstreams, `node --import tsx scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts --pricing --out v1.json --out-v2 v2.json`:
  - `main` (94fc0814ef6): exit 1, `models.dev catalog unavailable: Error: models.dev response exceeds 5242880 bytes` (same as the hosted runs).

- Regression test: a models.dev feed padded past 5 MiB (6 MiB, streamed without content-length) hydrates; a 40 MiB stream is rejected with `models.dev response exceeds 33554432 bytes` and cancelled before it is fully read. Against `main`'s script both cases fail (the 6 MiB feed hits the 5 MiB error).
- `vitest run test/scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 62 passed, 6.3 s (12.3 s wall). In CI (`checks-node-compact-small-2`) the two new cases took 44 ms and 29 ms.

fix: correct TIMESTAMP environment variable syntax in observe.sh

The inline environment variable syntax `TIMESTAMP="$timestamp" echo ...` 
does not work correctly because:
1. The pipe creates a subshell that doesn't inherit the variable
2. The environment variable is set for echo, not for the piped python

Fixed by using `export` and separating the commands:
- export TIMESTAMP="$timestamp"
- echo "$INPUT_JSON" | python3 -c "..."

This ensures the TIMESTAMP variable is available to the python subprocess.

fix(code-health): CRLF blobs measure like LF on Windows

Measurer.measure wrote each blob's decoded text into the temp tree with write_text's
default newline translation. On Windows that turns a CRLF blob into CR CR LF, so ruff
counted lines differently from the AST and comment tables: hits moved to <module>,
their `# health: allow` waivers were missed, and valid code blocked. Writing with
newline="" keeps the blob's own line endings. The test forces the Windows write
translation so it also runs on Linux.

fix(code-health): replay stops counting unmeasured PRs as clean

A manifest row whose range could not be built (base "", head "error: ...") or replayed
(an OID the clone does not have) was counted in the "N of M PRs had a blocking finding"
denominator with no findings, and the run exited 0, so a replay that measured nothing
read as evidence that a rule never fires. Such rows now carry an "error" in replay.jsonl,
stay out of the totals and the denominator, are listed by number, and fail the run.

fix(code-health): bound the cost of same-name pairing

Why (cost, same concern as Adolanium's line-matching note): pairing repeated names by body is
all-pairs within a group, and the per-group lookup of base units scanned the whole base file,
so a codemod touching every function of a big file was quadratic (5,000 edited unique names:
5.4 s -> 0.04 s with a per-file name index). A group whose all-pairs check would exceed
250,000 pairs (e.g. hundreds of edited `it(...)` callbacks in one scope) falls back to the
ordinal pairing, which is bounded; measured 2,000-callback group: 0.05 s.

fix(code-health): hits in a function moved and edited are placed by its origin's lines

Why (M2 follow-up; invariant 4, no trading): the previous commit let a moved+edited unit's
new-looking hits spend any departed occurrence of its origin unit by line text, so a swallow
dropped at the top of `legacy` paid for one added at the bottom of the moved copy (exit 0;
red on the previous commit), while the same relocation in place blocks. A unit matched
across files (pass 5) now compares its lines with its origin unit's (SequenceMatcher, code
only), exactly like an edit in place: hits on unchanged lines are old, the rest are new.
The departed-occurrence pool is now module-level only.

fix(code-health): a module-level hit moves only with its whole statement

Why (M1 follow-up; invariant 4, no trading): matching a departed module-level occurrence by
its line alone let `except Exception:` stand for any guard, so deleting
`try: import json / except Exception: pass` from one file paid for a new
`try: import yaml / except Exception: pass` in another (exit 0; red on the previous commit).
A module-level occurrence now moves only with its whole top-level statement unchanged
(found by indentation: a whole try/except block, or a one-line constant). Moving an unchanged
HX005 module constant to another file passes; a different constant still blocks.
Hits inside a unit matched across files keep line matching: only that unit's own departed
occurrences can pay.

fix(code-health): pair repeated names by body; keep the cap of a function moved and edited

Why:
- banditburai (inline, py_structure.py:97) and unsupportedpastels M3: repeated names (Python
  `@method(...) def _`, `f#2`; TS `<anon>#n`) were paired by source-order ordinal, so a new
  CC-22 `_` inserted above a trimmed one took its cap (exit 0), and inserting a small `_`
  above an unchanged CC-22 one made the old one "new" (exit 1). Same-file name matching now
  groups units by name without the ordinal and pairs the most similar bodies first
  (difflib ratio >= 0.6 over code lines, comments/whitespace dropped); the last unit left
  with a name is that name's unit, exactly as a unique name was before. Exact-hash passes
  still run first. If a body span is unknown, the group falls back to the ordinal.
- unsupportedpastels M2: cross-file matching was body-hash only, so a function moved to
  another file with one constant changed lost its cap (P1 exit 1; same edit in place exit 0).
  New last pass: another file, same name, similar body (>= 0.6), only when the name is gone
  from its origin file and exactly one unit of that name left and exactly one arrived
  unmatched. A copy (origin keeps it), two arrivals, or an unrelated body reusing a deleted
  name stay new code (andrexibiza: never arbitrary same-name credit). Its existing hits
  follow it through the departed-occurrence pool (one-to-one), a second swallow is new.
Unit gains an optional end_line; until the measurers report it (py_structure: lane A,
measure.py: lane C) the span is estimated from the unit's own FUNC_LINES. Tests pass both ways.

fix(code-health): module-level hits follow code moved to another file; skip idle line matching

Why (round-5 review, unsupportedpastels M1; Adolanium cost note):

fix(code-health): NESTING counts `else:` + indented `if` as nesting

JoaoMarcos44 (inline py_structure.py:49, review 5408439923; reproduced by
andrexibiza): nesting_depth() treated any If that sits alone in an orelse as
an `elif`, but `else:\n    if b:` produces the same AST. Seven physical
`else: if` levels measured 1 (adding an inert `pass` made them measure 7), so
the gate depended on an irrelevant statement rather than on indentation.

A real `elif` If node starts at the `elif` keyword, i.e. at its `if`'s
column; an `if` nested under `else:` must be indented deeper (a compound
statement cannot follow `else:` on the same line). Only the former keeps the
depth. Seven physical levels now measure 7 with or without the inert pass
and block; a genuine seven-arm elif chain stays at 1 and passes.

fix(code-health): recursive-rename normalization honours nested scopes (F15)

andrexibiza's F15 (changed form, inline on py_rules.py:250): body_hash()
disabled self-reference normalization whenever the textual dump contained
`arg('<name>'` or `Name('<name>', Store())` anywhere in the subtree, so an
unrelated nested `def identity(legacy)` made a pure recursive rename of
`legacy` lose its cap (FUNC_LINES 302 > target 300 as new code). Even with
the check removed, the string replace would also have blanked the nested
function's own `return legacy`, which refers to its parameter.

References are now resolved lexically: only bindings in the function's own
scope (params, assignments, nested def/class names, imports, global/nonlocal,
except/match captures) disable normalization, and a nested def/lambda/class/
comprehension that binds the name keeps its own reads. The matched Name /
Attribute nodes are blanked in place for the dump and restored. Controls: a
rename that leaves the old self-call is different code, an own-scope rebinding
is not a self-reference, a closure's call to its enclosing function is.

fix(code-health): HX005 evaluates annotations when the interpreter does (F9)

andrexibiza's F9 (changed form, inline on py_rules.py:250): definition
traversal kept a def's decorators and defaults but dropped its parameter and
return annotations, which run at def time on 3.11-3.13 (the project floor is
3.11) unless the module has `from __future__ import annotations`; measured on

`x: os.getenv("PATH")` annotation is never evaluated but the whole AnnAssign
was walked, so it was charged as a capture.

Def annotations now count as import-time exprs unless annotations are
postponed; an AnnAssign contributes its target and value always and its
annotation only when not postponed. A nested def's annotations stay out
(they run when the outer function does).

fix(code-health): HX009 follows annotated results and projects loop positions

Adolanium (comment 5983756525 §4) and JoaoMarcos44/andrexibiza: an annotated
`results: list = await asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` was not
recognised as a gather result (only ast.Assign was), so a plain `: list`
annotation hid the exact pattern HX009 exists for. Conversely, unpacking a
zip/enumerate tainted every loop variable, so `isinstance(payload, Exception)`
over `zip(payloads, results)` or the `i` of `enumerate(results)` was flagged.

AnnAssign values now propagate results, and loop/comprehension targets are
projected positionally: each element of a zip follows its own argument, an
enumerate taints only its item. Non-tuple targets keep the old whole-target
behaviour.

fix(code-health): HX006 post-kill exemption covers returned and annotated waits

JoaoMarcos44 (inline py_rules.py:442, review 5408210901; reproduced by
andrexibiza): after `proc.kill()` only an expression or plain-assignment
`proc.wait()` was recognised as reaped, so `return proc.wait()` and
`rc: int = proc.wait()` were flagged while the identical `rc = proc.wait()`
passed, and refactoring an accepted assignment into a return gained a blocker.

Return and AnnAssign values now count as the adjacent wait. The negative
controls stay flagged: no preceding kill, a different killed receiver,
communicate() after kill, and asyncio Process.wait() after kill; an explicit
finite timeout is still accepted. The assignment->return refactor is covered
through the real comparison path.

fix(code-health): track HX006 process handles per lexical scope

Adolanium (comment 5983756525 §4), corroborated by andrexibiza (F13 receiver
class) and helix4u: _process_handles() keyed handles by variable spelling for
the whole module, so an async `proc` in one function made a correctly bounded
sync `proc.communicate(timeout=1)` in another function fail HX006 (and a
`def stop(proc)` parameter inherited whatever `proc` meant elsewhere).

A plain-name handle now belongs to the scope that binds it: the innermost
scope binding the name decides (class bodies are invisible to methods,
closures see their enclosing function), and within it the latest binding
before the call, so reassignment (Popen -> asyncio process -> None)
re-classifies the receiver. Parameters and other bindings clear it. Attribute
handles (`self._proc`) stay shared by the methods of their class, keyed by
that class rather than by spelling across the module.

fix(code-health): report every independent import-time capture (F19)

andrexibiza's F19 (review 5407834086, inline): _capture_lines() returned after
the first eager capture it met. The reverse stack reaches an existing dict
entry first, so inserting `"new": os.getenv("HOME"),` above
`"old": os.getenv("PATH"),` produced no new HX005 occurrence and the
comparison could not charge it.

Every independent capture is now emitted (dict entries, list items, defaults);
a capture nested inside another (`expanduser(getenv(...))`) is the same
occurrence and is not entered, and per-line duplicates still collapse in the
measurer. Deferred bodies stay excluded. Tested through the real comparison
path: added dict/list/default captures block, a lambda entry and unchanged
debt pass, a separate assignment blocks.

fix(code-health): resolve import aliases per lexical scope (F12)

andrexibiza's F12 (changed form, review 5407834086): canonical_tree() pooled
every parameter, assignment and def in the module into one "rebound" set, so
`from subprocess import run as execute` stopped resolving everywhere as soon
as an unrelated function had a parameter or local named `execute`, and
`launch(cmd): return execute(cmd)` lost its HX006.

Bindings are now recorded per scope (module, class, function/lambda,
comprehension) and each read resolves through the scope chain the way Python
does: the innermost scope that binds the name decides, a scope that binds it
other than by one import makes it a plain local there, class bodies are not
visible to nested functions. Genuine shadowing in the consuming function (or
at module level) still stops resolution.

fix(code-health): replay samples a closed merge window and writes a manifest

The replay picked PRs with sort:updated-desc, so the sample changed whenever an old PR got a

fix(code-health): HX006 accepts proc.wait() right after proc.kill()

longer needs a timeout. communicate() after kill() and asyncio's

fix(code-health): occurrence provenance, alias-aware rules, strict file cap (round 4)

Fourth review round (F11-F18, N1-N4, kvnloo, Adolanium):

- Hits are old only where the base occurrence survives: a line the comment- and
  whitespace-blind line diff keeps (blame semantics), or anything inside a unit whose
  body is unchanged. An identical violation moved past unrelated code is new; removing
  an allow comment or re-indenting is not. Hit fingerprints exclude comments (N4).
- Inline allows cover their own line; only a comment-only line covers the next (N3).
- Rules read a copy of the AST with import aliases resolved, so `sp.run`,
  `from subprocess import run as execute`, aliased threading/asyncio/load_config are
  seen (F12); deadline helpers must resolve to the real asyncio API, and
  communicate()/wait() are judged only on receivers holding a spawned process (F13);
  infinite deadlines are unbounded (F14).
- HERMES_* writes introduce a name too (N1); bool(os.environ[...]) is HX010 (N2);
  HX009 needs the isinstance subject to come from gather(return_exceptions=True).
- Recursive self-references are normalised out of body hashes, so a recursive rename
  keeps its cap, py and ts (F15). Decorators belong to their function's scope and
  classes are matchable units, so their hits follow proven moves (F16).
- An over-cap file may not grow (F17, Teknium: strict improvement-only).
- A file the checker cannot parse or measure (ast/ruff/TS parse error) fails.
- scripts/check: --staged always lints an index snapshot (ignored files are invisible
  to git status, not to guards) (F18); create the --prefix dir for Git for Windows
  (F11); --only builds just the selected jobs, so it needs no ruff for non-ruff checks.

  Python-only lint jobs again and run only the ratchet.

fix(code-health): execution-scope-aware rule walks; BOM-stable git reads

Final review on #132646 (R1-R4), each reproduced on d03b089 first:

- Git blobs decode as utf-8-sig like working-tree reads, so a BOM no
  longer makes one side unparseable: a new BOM file's debt is measured
  (the hook used to let it through) and existing BOM debt is not new (R1).
- One walker, _eager(), yields what evaluating a node runs now: a
  lambda/def contributes only its defaults and decorators, a generator
  only its first iterable. HX005, HX006 and HX007 all use it, so a
  coroutine defined inside `asyncio.timeout()` is not treated as bounded
  and a returned sync loader is not a sync call in the coroutine (R2).
- `wait_for(fut=..., timeout=...)` is recognized like the positional
  form (R3).
- HX005 also checks lambda defaults, `if`/`while` tests, `with` context
  expressions, match guards and walrus bindings; a generator's body stays
  deferred (R4).

fix(code-health): one-to-one move matching, real deadlines, index-exact hook

Second-round review on #132646 (F1-F10), each reproduced on 2531fb2 first:

- Moves are matched one-to-one: unchanged units are reserved first, then
  same-file body, then cross-file body only when the origin's name is gone,
  then same name. A copy of unchanged debt is new debt; a function moved
  over a same-name stub keeps its own cap (F1, F3).
- Every base hit is owned by exactly one head scope, so a file rename no
  longer counts each old hit twice (F2).
- Ruff runs when either side has Python, so a delete-only .py diff with a
  TS edit no longer crashes on a missing ruff result (F4).
- Deadlines must be finite: timeout=None, **{} and asyncio.timeout(None)
  are no deadline; awaited calls inside `async with asyncio.timeout(x)`
  are bounded (F5, F8).
- HX005 walks only what runs at import: the import-time branch of a
  `__name__` guard (either operator), loops, match, try*, decorators,
  class bases; a lambda value is deferred (F9).
- `health: allow` counts only in real comment tokens (Python tokenize, TS
  comment trivia), never in string literals (F7).
- TS function lines are owned by the innermost function, so siblings on
  one line give it up once (F10).
- The pre-commit hook runs `scripts/check --staged`: health compares the
  index tree, and when the working tree differs from the index the other
  checkers run on a checkout-index copy with a copied index, so commits are
  judged on the staged bytes and unstaged work is never touched (F6).

fix(code-health): hits follow proven moves only; stable TS identity; show advisories

Independent review of #132646 found five defects, each reproduced and fixed:

- Pattern hits from any vanished scope went into a shared (rule, text) pool, so deleting one

- A unit's prior is now looked up by body hash before qualname, so a TS anonymous callback

- The TS body hash included the function name; it is now parameters + body, so a rename keeps

- HX006 flagged `await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=...)`; calls passed to

scripts/code_health measures the files a change touches on both sides

fix(tui_gateway): reopen the finalized row in the compute-host child, not _run_prompt_submit

The first attempt (a314952289) reopened in _run_prompt_submit's row-binding
block. Two contracts broke:

- Routing provenance (#106459): a turn on a still-registered session must NOT
  clear lineage/boundary stamps (compression, session_reset, new_session,
  ws_disconnect) — only a stale explicit close is cleared, by
  _reopen_routed_session_row under _sessions_lock, after the registration
  check. A blanket reopen earlier in the dispatch wiped deliberate stamps

- The bot-relay delivery harness rebinds _run_prompt_submit with a minimal
  globals set (no _session_db/_reopen_if_finalized) — NameError
  (test_bot_live_owner_delivery).

The seam was over-broad anyway: every real first turn crosses prompt.submit,
which now reopens both inline (persist path) and before the isolated dispatch.
What actually needs a second site is the compute-host CHILD: it builds its own
session record and writes the turn's transcript, so it reopens right next to
its existing _ensure_session_db_row binding in compute_host._run_real_turn —
module-qualified on server (no rebind hazard) and inside the same
contextlib.suppress (best-effort, like the row binding itself). The parent
already reopened before dispatch; the child's reopen is the belt-and-suspenders
half for an old parent or a synthesized re-entry.

fix(tui_gateway): reopen a finalized row before the isolated compute-host dispatch too (#85303 review)

_reopen_if_finalized lived only in _persist_session_row_for_submit, but the
isolated dispatch returns from prompt.submit BEFORE that persist (the child
process runs the turn), so an isolated first turn wrote its transcript into a
row still marked ended_at — exactly the stranded-row shape the review on
#128508 flagged.

Cover the seam at both dispatch sites:
- prompt.submit: reopen before _submit_prompt_to_compute_host. The turn is
  already admitted there (running, in flight, active-slot lease, truncation
  applied inline), so the child's writes must land in a live row.
- _run_prompt_submit row-binding block: reopen alongside _ensure_session_db_row.
  This is the one seam every turn crosses — inline dispatch, the compute-host
  child (_run_real_turn calls it directly), and the synthesized turns
  (auto-continue, queued drain, wake-ups) that bypass prompt.submit entirely.

Both are idempotent (helper no-ops on a live row) and best-effort like the
helper itself. A queued-prompt drain can never be the first turn after mount
(admission requires running=True from an accepted turn, which reopens), so no
third site is needed.

Review follow-up on the bare stdio PATH fix (#125318):

- `_first_user_which_hit` reused `_npx_bin_candidates`, whose Windows
  candidate list is the npx cache layout's `.cmd`/`.exe` pair. A user
  install that only ships a `.bat`/`.py` wrapper (stock PATHEXT carries
  both) was never found, so the scan returned None and silently fell
  back to the managed hit — the #125300 symptom persisted for those
  installs. Candidates now come from `_pathext_suffixes`: the child
  env's PATHEXT first (shutil.which reads the PARENT's, same source
  rationale as `_which_with_config_pathext`), then the parent's, then
  the OS default; a command that already carries a PATHEXT suffix is
  matched as written.
- The new `_bare_` test fixtures wrote extensionless executables, which
  `shutil.which` can never resolve on win32 (PATHEXT suffixes only), so
  the tests could only pass on POSIX and the Windows lane skipped the
  marker-less file entirely. Fixtures are now platform-shaped via
  `_bare_exe` (`python3.exe` on Windows, bare name + 0o755 elsewhere),
  and a direct `_first_user_which_hit` unit test covers the
  PATHEXT-driven candidate walk cross-platform.

interpreter — which lacks the user's packages and dies on import, while
the agent log only said "Connection closed" (#125300).

  the user's own hit for bare commands; the explicit launcher family

  managed hit rather than failing

fix(update): run the libatomic pre-install spawn only on Linux

The extra interpreter spawn ran on every platform before run_completion's
Popen. On Windows it went through subprocess.run first, which the taskkill
interrupt tests patch to assert only the completion child exists, so all
three failed. install_before_lock is a no-op off Linux anyway; skip the
spawn there.

chore(update): don't write old-interpreter bytecode into the new tree

The libatomic pre-install spawn now passes -B, matching the completion
child, which keeps its bytecode out of the checkout.

fix(update): keep the completion parent stdlib-only around the libatomic pre-install

run_completion runs in the OLD process after the checkout swap, and its
contract is never to import application helpers from the replacement tree.
Importing pm.libatomic there crashed the update when the new tree lacked
the module (downgrade or older pin) and on architectures where
current_target() raises. Run the pre-install as its own process from the
new tree, ignore its outcome, and let the in-lock repair report.

Also: gate on an openable /dev/tty first (cheapest check, and the detached
child exits immediately), treat an unsupported architecture as "skip",
bound the sudo -n probe, and drop the timeout on the interactive install
so a slow prompt or mirror is never killed mid-dpkg (it runs outside PM's
lock). Found in the final-head review of #132664.

fix(pm): install libatomic before the detached update child, not a sudo ticket

hermes update's completion runs PM in a start_new_session child with no
controlling terminal, so the in-child sudo -v warm-up could never read a
password and the cold password-sudo update from #124926 still failed. A
cached ticket was also the wrong currency: under sudo's default per-tty
timestamps a ticket minted in one session is not visible to another.

Install the package itself, interactively, at the last point that still
owns the terminal: run_completion() before it detaches, plus the existing
ensure_tools_for_sync() entry for the other update paths. Gate on an
openable /dev/tty instead of isatty() (a detached child inherits a tty
stdin and a forwarded-isatty stdout). Inside PM's lock the repair is
unchanged: sudo -n, stdin closed. Reported by @JoaoMarcos44 on #132664.

docs(install): document the libatomic host package step

Prerequisites now say the installer and hermes update install the distro
package providing libatomic.so.1 (sudo -n, one interactive prompt before
dependencies, never under --non-interactive), and the service-user section
no longer claims the installer provides no package-manager sudo step.

refactor(pm): prompt for sudo only when the repair would use it

The update warm-up resolved sudo on its own, so on a glibc host with no
supported package manager it still asked for a password the repair then
never used. Derive the prompt from the same _host_install_command and
_command_plan the repair runs, compute the target once, and correct the
module docstring now that there are two entry points.

fix(pm): let hermes update authorize sudo before restaging Node

The libatomic repair can only use sudo -n under PM's install lock, and
hermes update enters PM directly without install.sh's prerequisites
warm-up, so a cold password-sudo host still failed the update from
#124926. Before publishing tools, ask once on an interactive glibc host
that still lacks libatomic.so.1 and whose sudo would prompt. Reported by
@JoaoMarcos44 on #132664.

fix(install): never prompt for sudo under --non-interactive

The libatomic sudo warm-up checked only for a terminal, so
--non-interactive, -NonInteractive and --skip-setup still reached
`sudo -v </dev/tty` inside an SSH session or any PTY-allocating runner.
Gate it on NON_INTERACTIVE like setup and gateway. Reported by
@JoaoMarcos44 on #132664.

test: allowlist pm/libatomic's host package-manager lookups

The libatomic repair asks PATH for the distro package manager and sudo.
Those are host tools, not Hermes-managed runtimes, so a bare which is the
right question; PM also runs before hermes_platform is importable.

fix(install): keep the cached sudo ticket alive until PM runs

The clone and downloads can outlast sudo's timestamp_timeout, after which
PM's sudo -n repair silently falls back to the manual remedy. Refresh the
ticket non-interactively right before PM installs. Compute the bootstrap
target once in stage_prerequisites.

fix(pm): carry the libatomic remedy as InstallError's remedy

The hook glued the remedy into the reason, so the error ended with two
fixes, the second ("retry, or run hermes pm doctor") wrong for a missing
host library. Return (reason, remedy) and pass the remedy through. When the
package installs but Node still cannot load it, say that instead of telling
the user to run the command that just succeeded.

perf(pm): attempt the libatomic install once per process

Every root that depends on node (npm, browser tools) re-stages it after a
failure, so a host without libatomic ran the package manager under PM's
install lock once per dependent root. Cache the outcome for the process.
Also use platform.freedesktop_os_release() instead of a hand parser, and
run apt-get update once when a minimal image has empty package lists.

fix(install): ask for sudo up front when Node will need libatomic

PM's libatomic repair runs `sudo -n` under its install lock, so on a host
whose sudo needs a password the automatic attempt can never succeed and
`curl | bash` still ends in "pm install failed". When the glibc host lacks
libatomic.so.1 and a terminal is attached, cache sudo credentials during
the prerequisites stage so the later non-interactive install goes through.
Root, passwordless sudo, musl, and headless runs are unchanged.

test(pm): keep the two libatomic invariant tests

Install-time repair re-probes after installing the host package, and the
automatic attempt never reads a TTY (sudo -n, stdin closed) while PM holds
its install lock. The remaining cases pinned helper internals; one also
failed whenever the pytest tmp path contained the word libatomic.

fix: send_message to a Home Assistant target names the install command while its plugin is absent
