"Unknown or unregistered plugin platform: homeassistant" and no way forward.

Both unknown-platform errors (target resolution and platform config) now go through one helper
that appends, for a platform that left core (a LEFT_CORE row's platform), the exact install
command for the active home (`hermes [-p <profile>] plugins install homeassistant`). Other unknown
names keep the bare message.

fix: an offline machine pays the Home Assistant plugin fetch once an hour, not every start

While the plugin was missing and the catalog or GitHub unreachable, every `hermes chat` process
paid a live-catalog fetch (+5.9 s on a blackholed network) and printed the raw multi-line git
stderr of the failed clone.

A failed automatic install (catalog miss, failed install) touches
<home>/cache/left-core-<plugin>.failed; agent and gateway start skip the row, before any network,
while that stamp is under an hour old. `hermes update` ignores the stamp and always retries. The
failure notice is one line: git's own fatal:/error: line when the error carries raw git output,
else its first line.

The catalog module already serves a fresh cache (6 h) and falls back to its stale/in-tree copy on
failure; pre-resolving offline would not save the round trip, because the install resolves the
entry through the live catalog again, so the gate sits before both.

fix: a removed Home Assistant plugin stays removed after update and restart

The left-core migration's only gate was "plugin dir missing + Home Assistant in use", so after
`hermes plugins remove homeassistant` every agent start, gateway start and `hermes update`
reinstalled and re-enabled it (~7.5 s each).

The automatic install now happens at most once per home and row: `_left_core_installed` in
config.yaml is written (in the same write as the toolset-scope marker when the plugin was already
there, right after a successful install otherwise) and only once the plugin dir exists in that
home. A marked row is never installed again; a catalog miss, failed install or lazy-installs-off
start writes nothing, so those homes keep retrying. Profile clones copy plugins/ with config.yaml,
so a clone's marker always matches what its source had.

fix: a channel-less profile clone drops Home Assistant identity while its plugin is absent

Profile cloning learns which env keys and config blocks belong to a messaging channel from core's
platform registry. Moving Home Assistant into a plugin left that ownership only on the loaded
plugin, so while the migration is pending (catalog miss, offline, lazy installs off, declined),
`hermes profile create X --clone` kept HASS_TOKEN/HASS_URL and the gateway.homeassistant block in
the clone while printing "Messaging channels were NOT cloned (homeassistant)". The copied token
then reads as Home Assistant in use, so the clone would migrate onto the source's HA identity.

LEFT_CORE rows now declare the channel ownership core had for their platform: enable_env (the env
that enabled the adapter) and channel_env_prefixes (prefixes shared with the plugin's tools).
profile_channels includes those platforms in platform_ids, the shared-prefix rule, the enable-gate
and the duplicate-credential inventory regardless of plugin installation, so the source-runs-the-
adapter rule is exactly core's: enabled (config or HASS_TOKEN) -> stripped; explicitly disabled,
tool-only -> HASS_* kept as a tool credential.

fix: a preinstalled Home Assistant plugin no longer turns its tools on everywhere

The migration converts core's per-platform Home Assistant tool scope (off on telegram: [web], acp,
webhook) into known_plugin_toolsets entries, but only on the install branch: a home whose plugin
directory already existed returned before the conversion. The official plugin stays inert on a core
that still bundles HA, so a user who installed it before updating (or a partial earlier run) kept no
exclusions, and after the update the plugin toolset came on for every platform.

Installation and the one-time policy conversion are now separate: every home that uses the feature
gets the conversion once per row, plugin present or not, and the completion is recorded under
_left_core_scoped in the same config.yaml write. A later run (update, agent/gateway start) skips
it, so a choice the user makes afterwards (`hermes tools` enabling HA on telegram) is never undone.

fix: Home Assistant migration reads the platform config the gateway loader merged

The left-core migration decided "this home used Home Assistant" with its own config reader: the
first platforms.homeassistant block in config.yaml. The pre-extraction gateway enabled the adapter
from more places: the legacy gateway.json base layer, the gateway.homeassistant shorthand, and
nested gateway.platforms + top-level platforms blocks merged key by key. Those homes got no plugin
and no notice, and lost Home Assistant on update.

platform_configured_on() now asks the gateway loader itself: load_legacy_gateway_json +
read_yaml_layers (managed overlay, ${VAR} expansion) + merge_platform_sections, then
PlatformConfig.from_dict for the enabled flag, so the last explicit `enabled` keeps winning
(config.yaml enabled: false over a gateway.json enable stays not-in-use).
merge_platform_sections takes `also=` so the gateway.<platform> shorthand of a platform that
left core counts before its plugin registers (Platform() no longer knows the name).

fix: agent-start left-core migration tolerates agents without a startup-warning sink

With the try/except gone, stub agents (SimpleNamespace in tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py)
raised AttributeError on the say= argument before recover_at_startup ran.

fix: every profile a multiplex gateway serves gets its left-core plugin before its adapters start

Gateway start ran the left-core migration only for the launch home, so a secondary profile that
used Home Assistant as its event platform started without the plugin and without its adapter (and a
named launcher's default-root primary was never migrated). Each secondary now runs the migration in
its own runtime scope before its plugins are discovered, and gateway start covers the launch home and
the default root (the multiplex primary). The gateway-start helpers live in gateway/run_startup.py;
run.py and agent_init.py lose the try/except wrappers, since recover_at_startup never raises.

An agent-start install of a row that ships a platform now tells the user to restart the gateway
when one serves the home: the running gateway loaded its platforms before the plugin existed.

fix: a user plugin cannot mark a core platform trusted_inbound

PluginContext.register_platform is last-writer-wins, so a user plugin could re-register 'telegram'
with trusted_inbound=True and every sender would skip the allowlist and pairing. The flag is now
refused for a platform core ships (a static Platform member or a bundled plugins/platforms/ plugin)
unless the registering plugin is bundled. Home Assistant is no longer either, so its catalog plugin
keeps it. `hermes plugins validate` prints a line for every trusted_inbound platform (and fails one
naming a core platform).

Also: the MCP collision test docstring no longer refers to the toolset it used to collide with.

fix: Home Assistant tools stay off on platforms where core had them off

Core's homeassistant toolset was on for a platform only when its saved platform_toolsets list (or
its default composite) carried it. As a plugin toolset it is on for every platform whose
known_plugin_toolsets does not name it, so a user who scoped HA out of Telegram with
`platform_toolsets.telegram: [web, terminal, file]` got device control there after the migration;
webhook and acp, whose default composites never carried it, gained it too.

Left-core rows now name their toolsets and the platforms whose default composite lacked them. Before
any install (automatic or the user's own) the migration records the toolsets in
known_plugin_toolsets[platform] wherever core resolved them off; platforms core had them on for are

Moving HA out of core dropped HASS_TOKEN/HASS_URL from the static provider blocklist and HASS_TOKEN

fix(desktop): re-check primary ownership after the reconnect ticket mint

Both primary recovery paths fenced the route lookup but not the WebSocket
ticket mint that follows it. When a connection apply (boot hook) or a
foreground activation (request recovery) landed while the ticket was in
flight and the newer socket had already dropped, the stale attempt dialed the
old primary route. connect() no-ops on an open socket, so the gap only shows
once the applied socket is closed, but then it re-attached the window to the
gateway the user had just left.

The boot reconnect now compares the route revision it recorded against the
current one again before dialing; request recovery re-checks ownsForeground().

fix(desktop): keep a stale primary recovery from overwriting the foreground descriptor

useGatewayRequest's primary recovery resolves the connection profile-less, so
main answers through the window's CURRENT route. When the user activated
another source while that lookup was in flight, the late answer was published
with setConnection() over the newer foreground descriptor (and a failed
lookup cleared it), so REST and filesystem helpers routed to the old backend
while the newer source was in front.

Recovery now snapshots the gateway activation epoch and publishes, clears, or
dials only while the primary still owns the foreground. The boot hook's
own-route reconnect loop keeps restoring the primary socket, and the replay
guard already refuses to resend the original request.

fix(desktop): drop a primary reconnect lookup a connection apply replaced

Address review on #132237: an in-flight primary reconnect whose route lookup
resolved after a connection apply recorded its old descriptor over the newly
applied primary. The next socket drop then dialed the old gateway by its
explicit route, where the profile-less lookup on base followed the applied
window route.

Every primary route record now bumps a revision; a reconnect snapshots it
before the lookup and drops the result if a boot or apply recorded a newer
route meanwhile, so it no longer records, publishes or dials the old route.
The source-qualified primary lookup is unchanged.

fix(desktop): keep a newer new-chat draft from a late switch re-home

Address the ordinary-switch draft-intent race from review on #132237: a
draft started on another gateway while a source switch was still doing its
bookkeeping (rememberConnection) was cleared by the switch's late re-home,
so the next session.create went to the switched-to source instead.

Every new-chat owner intent goes through captureNewChatSource, which now
bumps an intent revision. selectConnection snapshots it when the switch
starts and only re-homes the draft if no newer intent arrived, so a newer
intent wins even when it repeats the same route values. Completed switches
with no newer intent re-home as before.

fix(desktop): keep review-flagged owner rules in the gateway-switch fixes

Address review on #132237:

- Project-tree rows go through the canonical stampRowsWithOwningConnection:
  a row that already names an owner is never re-owned, and local stays bare
  on the primary path so the legacy profile door (#94166) is unchanged. local
  is stamped only when it is an active registry secondary.
- Resume remembers an ambient owner hint only for a row that actually
  resolved; an unresolved id no longer gets pinned to the foreground source.
- The silent boot restore keeps an explicit new-chat route pinned while it
  was in flight; the route clear lives in one helper.

  paths resolve differently.

fix(desktop): reconnect the primary socket to its own route, not the foreground

Primary reconnect called profile-less getConnection(), which main resolves from
the window's foreground route. A drop while a secondary was foregrounded
re-dialed the primary socket to that secondary's backend. Reconnect by the
primary's recorded registry route (or legacy profile); boot and connection
apply keep following the foreground.

fix(desktop): never replay a failed RPC on a different gateway

useGatewayRequest recovered a transport failure through the current active
route and retried the original payload there. A gateway switch between
dispatch and the delayed rejection replayed the request on the other source.
Retry only while the dispatch route is still active; otherwise surface the
original error.

Resume kept the ambient connection only for remote mode, so an untagged row
while This device was an active registry secondary reduced to a bare profile
and routed to the window primary. Keep the legacy primary-local profile door
(#94166) unchanged, and remember the resolved owner for later prompts.

fix(process_registry): stop systemd-run expanding scoped commands (#132385)

Since systemd 254, `systemd-run --scope` expands $VAR / ${VAR} / $$ in the
command line itself (--expand-environment defaults to yes), so a background
command under a supervised gateway ran rewritten: `$$` became a literal `$`,
`${arr[@]}` became '' with a warning on stderr.

option (and never expanded in scope mode), so the existing cached probe drops
it and re-probes once when systemd-run names it in the rejection — no extra
subprocess on modern hosts and no lost isolation on old ones.

fix(process_registry): drop dashboard/serve worker scoping; make the hang test catch the hang

Scoping a supervised dashboard/serve backend's background processes moved them out of the
backend's service cgroup, so they survived a backend restart, but nothing in dashboard/serve
startup recovers the process checkpoint: they kept running while process list/poll/kill could
not find them, and the next spawn dropped their checkpoint record. Recovering them in serve
would conflict with the gateway owning background processes (#106742). Revert to main's
behaviour for dashboard/serve (workers stay in the backend's cgroup and die with it) and leave
escapee cleanup there to the serve-to-gateway cutover.

Tests: the escapee in the hang test printed before the kill deadline, which ended the reader's
blocked read and let the old close finish in time, so the test passed without the fix. The hang
test's escapee is now silent; late-output rejection has its own test. Removing the reader-close
guard now fails the hang test.

fix(process_registry): decide a killed PTY chunk atomically with the kill

The reader checked session.exited and then appended, so a chunk read before
the kill could pass the check, lose the CPU while kill_process snapshotted the
output and set exited, and then land in the killed session (and be streamed)
after the kill returned.

ProcessSession.append_output_if_running() checks exited and appends under the
same session lock the kill holds for its snapshot, and _ingest_output(...,
unless_exited=True) only scans and streams a chunk it admitted. A chunk is now
either in the kill's receipt or dropped. The pipe reader is unchanged.

Tests: a deterministic regression pauses the reader between reading a chunk
and buffering it, runs the real kill, then resumes, and asserts the chunk is
in neither the receipt, the buffer nor the live stream. The escapee spawn
helper now terminates the PTY child it spawned if its readiness check fails.

fix(process_registry): freeze a killed PTY session's output; address review

Review follow-ups on the deferred PTY close:

- The reader can now outlive a kill while a detached descendant holds the
  slave open. It keeps draining, but no longer appends to or streams into the
  killed session, so the output stays as the kill reported it.
- The live-reader guard in _release_finished_handles is POSIX-only. pywinpty
  reads don't block, so Windows closes the PTY on the finish path as before.

Tests:
- The unscoped kill test has the escapee print after the kill and asserts the
  killed session never receives that output.
- New test_start_server_marks_the_process_as_backend_host drives the real
  web_server.start_server entry point, so removing the mark_backend_host()
  call fails a test.
- The live scope test bounds its escapee to 30 s and terminates the PTY child
  it spawned on failure (the reparented escapee is left to its bound).

test(process_registry): read the escapee pid without `$$` so the scoped case runs on systemd >= 254

`systemd-run --scope` expands the command line itself since systemd 254
(`--expand-environment` defaults to yes), so the `$$` in the escapee
command reached the shell as a literal `$` and the pidfile held `$\n`:
`test_scoped_backend_kill_reaps_an_escaped_descendant` failed with
`ValueError: invalid literal for int()` on any host where the live scope
test does not skip (systemd 259 here). Read the pid as a grandchild's
`$PPID` instead, which neither systemd-run nor the shell rewrites.

Review-fix commit on the contributor's branch; no source change.

fix(process_registry): scope background processes of a supervised dashboard/serve backend

Only the supervised messaging gateway ran background processes in their own
systemd scope (_is_supervised_gateway_process requires _HERMES_GATEWAY and the
gateway PID file). A dashboard or serve backend run by systemd hosts the same
kind of agent turns, but its background processes shared its cgroup, so a
descendant that setsid()s past the PTY/process-group kill survived it: the kill
reported success while the escapee kept running (and kept the PTY slave open).

web_server.start_server now marks the process as a backend host (process-local,
so terminal children and CLIs that inherit the supervisor env don't count), and
_scope_argv scopes when that host was launched by a service manager. The kill
already stops the scope, which reaps the whole cgroup. The self-kill guards that
also read _is_supervised_gateway_process are unchanged.

fix(process_registry): never close a PTY under its live reader thread

kill_process released the PTY master while the PTY reader thread was
still blocked in read(). ptyprocess wraps the master in a BufferedRWPair,
so close() waits on the buffer lock the reader holds, and that read only
ends when every holder of the slave side is gone. A descendant that
setsid()s past the kill keeps it open, so the kill never returned (and on
the TTL prune path the same close runs under ProcessRegistry._lock).

Leave the close to the reader while it is alive: its own teardown
(_finish_reader -> _move_to_finished) releases the PTY once its read ends.

details` -> `... details`; same for `Authorization: *** then prose`,
`X-Api-Key: *** (set in env)`). The scrub was not a fixed point.

optional `=` padding, then a token boundary) before `***` counts as a
masked scheme. The floor is 8, not 16, so 15-char keys still redact.

are stable over three passes.

so the scheme becomes `***` and the key is left in the text. The support scrub

x-auth-token families with Bearer/Basic/Digest, in both bare and `-H '...'`
forms. Base and main leak the same input.

That value must not be another secret header, so `x-api-key: *** cookie=...`
is not consumed. The key is redacted, and the redacted output is a fixed
point. The fix stays in the support layer. Teaching agent.redact the scheme
does not help, because its YAML/assignment passes mask the scheme word first.

feat(web): reveal a clipped sidebar session title on hover (#4423)

* feat(web): reveal a clipped sidebar session title on hover

A session title wider than its sidebar row is clipped with an ellipsis, so a
long parent title hides the `(1)` that distinguishes its fork. Hovering the row
now scrolls the title to its far edge and returns it to the start when the
pointer leaves. The title stays an `overflow: hidden` scrollport, so nothing
reflows and no scrollbar appears; `scroll-behavior: smooth` supplies the motion
(reduced motion keeps the jump), and the hovered row clips instead of
ellipsizing because a scrolled box still paints the ellipsis over the revealed
characters.

Covered by the row component spec, the stylesheet contract spec, and a new
keyless Chromium scenario that hovers a seeded clipped row in the assembled
application and asserts the reached scroll extent.

* fix(web): return the revealed session title in one step

Review follow-up on the hover reveal:

- Return the title to its start with `scrollTo({ behavior: 'instant' })` instead
  of a smooth scroll. A smooth return carried the resting ellipsis and the
  narrowing cell over the travelling text for its whole duration.
- Scope `scroll-behavior: smooth` to `.sessionRow .title` so Workspace rows are
  untouched, and fold the reduced-motion reset into the file's existing block.
- Guard the hover-only `text-overflow: clip` with `@media (hover: hover)`: a
  touch tap latches `:hover` after the title has already returned, which would
  otherwise strand that row without its ellipsis.
- Pin the contract in the browser scenario: computed `scroll-behavior` is
  `smooth` by default and `auto` under reduced motion, and the return lands
  inside one step. Add the unit case for the explicit instant return.
